title: Video: Phase 5 — Content Protection (Signed Playback)
description:
## Context
Video Phase 5 — content protection via signed playback. Currently all Mux videos use unsigned playback URLs, meaning anyone with the URL can watch without enrollment. For premium/restricted courses, this is unacceptable. Plan: specs/plans/video-pipeline-delivery_plan.md Phase 5.

## Outcome
- Server-side JWT token generation for Mux signed playback
- Token includes 12h expiry, domain restriction, and user context
- Enrollment check before token generation (unenrolled users get HTTP 403)
- Domain restriction limits playback to production URLs only
- ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK feature flag (default: off)
- Mux signing key stored in Infisical → GCP SM → ExternalSecrets

## Non-goals
- DRM (Widevine/FairPlay) — signed URLs are sufficient for MVP
- Offline video download with protection
- Per-video watermarking
- Geographic playback restrictions

## Constraints
- Mux Signing Keys require RSA 2048-bit key pair
- Token expiry must balance security (shorter) vs UX (longer) — 12h chosen
- Must not break unsigned playback for non-restricted courses
- Feature flag must be off by default until E2E validation

## Plan
1. Generate Mux Signing Key pair (RSA 2048-bit)
2. Store private key in Infisical → GCP SM → ExternalSecrets
3. Register public key with Mux API
4. Create token generation endpoint in LMS API
5. Add enrollment check middleware to token endpoint
6. Configure domain restriction for production URLs
7. Wire Video XBlock to request signed URL for restricted courses
8. Create feature flag ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a course is marked restricted and ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK is on, When an enrolled student plays a video, Then a signed playback URL with 12h expiry is generated
- Given a course is restricted, When an unenrolled user requests a playback token, Then HTTP 403 is returned
- Given a signed URL has expired, When a student tries to play the video, Then Mux returns 403 and the XBlock requests a fresh token
- Given domain restriction is configured, When the signed URL is used from a non-production domain, Then playback is blocked
- Given ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK is off, When any student plays a video, Then unsigned playback URLs are used

## Verification
```bash
# Signing key in ExternalSecrets
kubectl get secret mux-signing-key -n mereka-lms -o jsonpath='{.data.MUX_SIGNING_KEY}' | base64 -d | head -1

# Token endpoint
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" \
  "https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/mux/signed-url/?video_id=<playback_id>" | jq '.url'

# Unauthorized access
curl -sf "https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/mux/signed-url/?video_id=<playback_id>" # Should return 401

# Feature flag
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from waffle import flag_is_active; print(flag_is_active(None, 'ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK'))"
```

## Rollback
- Disable feature flag: ENABLE_MUX_SIGNED_PLAYBACK=False (instant)
- Falls back to unsigned playback URLs
- Signing key remains in ExternalSecrets (no cleanup needed)
- Mux-side signing key can be deactivated via API

## Observability
- Prometheus: mux_signed_tokens_generated_total, mux_signed_token_denied_total{reason}
- Alert: mux_signed_token_denied_rate > 20% (possible abuse)
- Grafana panel in Video Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "mux_signed" | logfmt`

## Security
- RSA 2048-bit signing key stored in ExternalSecrets (never in code)
- Token includes: playback_id, expiry, audience (domain), subject (user_id)
- Enrollment verified server-side before token generation
- Signing key rotation: generate new key, update ExternalSecrets, deactivate old key in Mux

## Docs
- docs/operations/VIDEO_PIPELINE_RUNBOOK.md (add content protection section)
- specs/video-pipeline-delivery_spec.md Phase 5 ACs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 4 analytics (mereka-lms-17jr)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal phase)
- Parent: mereka-lms-1bdm (Video epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead)

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='video' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Video implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: ArgoCD auto-sync does not reliably apply kustomize images transformer on promotion
description:
RESEARCH CORRECTION 2026-04-17:

CLASSIFICATION: governance/signal-hygiene — UNVERIFIED as defect. Correctly classified.

EVIDENCE:
- ONE occurrence (2026-04-17 ~03:50 UTC). Not a pattern.
- ArgoCD ApplicationSet has ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true — documented, intentional.
- Site-down runbook already states: 'If Argo reports Synced while stale config still serves, trigger one full sync with ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=false for that operation.'
- Standard ArgoCD reconciliation is 3-5 min polling. Timing mismatch is normal GitOps behavior.
- No evidence ApplyOutOfSyncOnly actually skips kustomize images transformer rendering.
- Force-sync fixed it immediately — consistent with reconciliation lag, not a rendering defect.

PROVING ACTION ON NEXT PROMOTION:
1. Merge a promotion that ONLY changes kustomize images
2. Wait 5 minutes without manual intervention
3. Check: did ArgoCD auto-apply the image change?
   - YES → close as one-time lag
   - NO (stale again) → escalate with reproduction proof, investigate ApplyOutOfSyncOnly + images transformer interaction

SHOULD SURVIVE: only if it reproduces on the next cycle.
notes: SCOPE: infra-only. ArgoCD Application defined in bbi-infrastructure. mereka-lms can only observe. Fix (if any) is in ArgoCD Application spec in bbi-infrastructure. Bead retained here as observation-only with infra ownership noted.
close_reason: ONE-TIME INCIDENT, not durable defect. ArgoCD dev app has automated sync (selfHeal=true, prune=true, ServerSideApply). Kustomize images transformer correctly configured. Drift check workflow runs automatically post-build. Most likely: operator force-synced before 3-min reconciliation window finished. Verify-argocd-drift.sh catches mismatches. No pattern of forced syncs documented.

8. Wait for Phase 4 SSO to unblock, then close

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given enterprise-catalog pod crashes, When it is down for >5m, Then PodDown alert fires in Alertmanager
- Given enterprise-access CPU exceeds 70%, When sustained for >5m, Then HPA scales from 1 to 2 replicas
- Given enterprise-subsidy memory exceeds 85% of limit, When sustained for 10m, Then MemoryHigh warning alert fires
- Given all 4 enterprise services are healthy, When checking ServiceMonitors, Then Prometheus scrapes metrics every 30s

## Verification
```bash

kubectl get servicemonitor -n mereka-lms | grep enterprise

# PrometheusRules

# HPAs

  "from waffle.models import Flag; print([f.name for f in Flag.objects.filter(name__contains='enterprise')])"
```

## Rollback
- Delete HPAs: `kubectl delete hpa -n mereka-lms -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=mereka-lms`
- Delete PrometheusRules: `kubectl delete prometheusrule enterprise-alerts -n mereka-lms`
- Delete ServiceMonitors: `kubectl delete servicemonitor -l service=enterprise -n mereka-lms`
- Remove waffle flags via LMS admin
- Services continue to run without monitoring/scaling

## Observability
- Prometheus: 16 enterprise alerts (PodDown, PodRestarting, MemoryHigh, CPUHigh x4 services)
- ServiceMonitors: scraping /health/ endpoints every 30s
- HPAs: CPU-based autoscaling with 300s scaledown stabilization

- No secrets exposed in monitoring configs
- HPA scaling bounded (max 3 replicas) to prevent resource exhaustion
- Enterprise API endpoints protected by JWT authentication

title: fix: MFE aggressive caching causes stale blank pages after deployments
description:
MFE micro-frontends aggressively cache static assets. After deployments, users see blank pages because stale JS bundles reference old chunk hashes that no longer exist on the server.

Root cause: Caddy/CDN caching headers set long max-age without proper cache-busting on deployment.

Fix options:
A) Add content-hash to MFE build output filenames (already done by webpack, but Caddy strips)
B) Configure Caddy to serve MFE assets with Cache-Control: no-cache for HTML, long-cache for hashed assets
C) Add deployment-time cache purge script

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-002: MFE JS/CSS assets served with content-hash in filename + long cache
- [ ] AC-003: Post-deployment smoke test confirms no blank pages

title: Email: Build Notification Pipeline (6 phases, 45 ACs)
description:
## Context
Email notification pipeline epic — 6-phase buildout from basic SMTP relay to full-featured notification system. Currently LMS sends email via SMTP relay with no bounce handling, no user preferences, no in-app notifications. 45 ACs across 6 phases. Spec: specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md (Tier 7). Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md (62 tasks, 16 weeks).

## Outcome
- SES production mode with DKIM/SPF/DMARC, bounce/complaint handling, suppression list
- User email preferences with GDPR consent tracking and one-click unsubscribe
- In-app notification center (notification store, REST API, real-time via WebSocket)
- Push notifications via FCM (iOS + Android)
- Multi-language email templates (EN/MS/ZH) with bulk campaign support
- Engagement analytics: open rate, click rate, unsubscribe rate per template
- 45/45 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- SMS notifications (separate channel, separate bead)
- WhatsApp integration (not in scope)
- Per-course notification rules (too granular for MVP)
- Third-party email marketing tools (Mailchimp, SendGrid)

## Constraints
- AWS SES Free Tier: 62,000 emails/month from EC2
- GDPR compliance required for EU users
- FCM requires Firebase project setup (iOS + Android certificates)
- Multi-language templates require translator coordination
- Budget: SES costs + FCM (free tier)

## Plan

title: Libraries: Enable Content Libraries v2 (33 ACs)
description:
## Context
Content Libraries v2 epic — enable and scale the Content Libraries v2 system across the platform. Spec: specs/content-libraries-v2_spec.md (Tier 7, 33 ACs). Plan: specs/plans/content-libraries-v2_plan.md (137 tasks, 4 phases, 12 weeks).

Content Libraries v2 enables reusable content blocks (OLX) that can be shared across multiple courses, reducing duplication and improving consistency. Without this, course authors must duplicate content blocks in each course, leading to maintenance overhead and inconsistent updates.

## Outcome
- Content Libraries v2 enabled by default in Ulmo — no waffle flag needed
- Platform library created: `lib:MEREKA:platform-templates` with 10 OLX content blocks
- Library published and accessible via REST API: GET /api/libraries/v2/
- library_content XBlock (`LegacyLibraryContentBlock`) available for cross-course reuse
- Meilisearch config committed for CMS (needs kustomize deploy to activate search indexing)
- All 4 phases complete: operator libraries, single-tenant, multi-tenant scale, hardening
- Backup and monitoring systems operational for library content

## Non-goals
- Migrating existing v1 library content to v2 automatically (manual migration required)
- Versioning of library content blocks (use Git for version control)
- WYSIWYG editor for library blocks (OLX editing only)
- Library content preview without course context

## Constraints
- Blockstore service must be deployed and healthy (dependency)
- Meilisearch deployment requires kustomize overlay apply (committed but not deployed)
- Phase 1 complete (commit 94e03de) — Phases 2-4 in progress
- Multi-tenant access controls require per-tenant organization filtering
- 12-week timeline for full 4-phase rollout

## Plan
1. Phase 0: Verify Blockstore + API baseline (bead mereka-lms-1k14)
2. Phase 1: Platform operator libraries (bead mereka-lms-11i7) — COMPLETE
3. Phase 2: Single-tenant enterprise libraries (bead mereka-lms-3oak)
4. Phase 3-4: Multi-tenant scale + hardening (bead mereka-lms-72yu)
5. Deploy CMS Meilisearch config to cluster (committed, not applied)
6. Conduct load testing for library sharing at scale
7. Document library authoring workflows for course creators

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given Content Libraries v2 is enabled, When a course author creates a new library, Then it is stored in Blockstore and accessible via REST API
- Given a library contains OLX blocks, When a course author inserts library_content XBlock, Then content is pulled from the library into the course
- Given Meilisearch is configured, When a user searches library content, Then results are returned from indexed library blocks
- Given a library is updated, When a course references that library, Then changes propagate to all courses using that content
- Given multi-tenant mode is enabled, When a tenant creates a library, Then only that tenant can access the library content

## Verification
```bash
# Phase 1 verification (COMPLETE — commit 94e03de)
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/cms -- python manage.py cms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.content_libraries.models import ContentLibrary; print(ContentLibrary.objects.filter(slug=\"platform-templates\").exists())"

# Blockstore service health
kubectl get pods -n mereka-lms -l app.kubernetes.io/name=blockstore

# Meilisearch config committed (not deployed)
git log --oneline infrastructure/tutor/plugins/mfe/patches/meilisearch-config.yml

# REST API accessibility
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $LMS_TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/libraries/v2/

# Library content XBlock available
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from xmodule.library_content_block import LegacyLibraryContentBlock; print(LegacyLibraryContentBlock.__name__)"
```

## Rollback
- Phase 1 rollback: Delete platform library via Django admin or REST API
- Disable Content Libraries v2: Set waffle flag `content_libraries_v2.enabled` to False
- Remove Meilisearch config: Revert kustomize overlay changes
- Blockstore rollback: Scale deployment to 0 replicas (data preserved in persistent volume)
- No data loss — library content stored in Blockstore (persistent storage)

## Observability
- Prometheus: library_api_requests_total{endpoint,method,status}, library_content_blocks_total, blockstore_storage_bytes
- Alert: library_api_error_rate > 5% for 15m, blockstore_pod_down for 5m
- Grafana panel: Content Libraries Dashboard (library creation rate, storage usage, API latency)
- Loki: `{namespace="mereka-lms",app="cms"} |~ "content_libraries|blockstore" | logfmt`

## Security
- Library access controlled by Django permissions (staff only for platform libraries)
- Multi-tenant access enforced via organization filtering (Phase 3)
- REST API requires authentication token
- OLX content sanitized to prevent XSS in library blocks
- Audit log for library creation/modification (Django admin log)

- docs/features/CONTENT_LIBRARIES_V2.md (to create — usage guide for course authors)

title: Adopt bv robot protocol as standard agent workflow
description:
We have bv installed but are NOT using its graph-aware capabilities. The beads_viewer README describes a complete agent workflow we're ignoring.

- **bv installed**: Yes (v0.14.x)
- **Labels on beads**: ZERO. 0 out of 73 open beads have labels. This kills bv's label-health, label-flow, label-attention features entirely.
- **Acceptance Criteria in beads**: Only NEW beads (from today's session) have ACs. Old beads (P0/P1 epics like Velero DR, MongoDB, Domain Readiness) have ZERO ACs.
- **bv blurb in AGENTS.md**: Missing. Agents don't know bv exists.

title: Mobile: Phase 2 — iOS Stabilization (PKCE, Token Lifecycle, Push, TestFlight)
description:
## Context
iOS app needs OAuth 2.0 + PKCE authentication, secure token lifecycle management, push notification integration, and a TestFlight CI/CD pipeline. Without PKCE and proper token handling, the iOS app cannot securely authenticate users or maintain sessions across app restarts and backgrounding.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-MOB-008: OAuth 2.0 + PKCE flow via ASWebAuthenticationSession stores tokens in iOS Keychain
- [ ] AC-MOB-009: Proactive token refresh triggers <5min before expiry with single-flight (no duplicate refreshes)
- [ ] AC-MOB-010: 401 response triggers one refresh attempt; failure redirects to login (no infinite retry loop)
- [ ] AC-MOB-011: Logout revokes tokens server-side and clears Keychain
- [ ] AC-MOB-012: Push notification tap navigates to correct course/lesson content
- [ ] AC-MOB-013: GitHub Actions builds and uploads to TestFlight within 30 minutes of main branch push
- [ ] AC-MOB-014: No tokens or secrets logged to console or crash reports
- [ ] AC-MOB-015: App snapshot cleared on background (privacy protection)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-ios-auth.sh\` (PKCE flow + token lifecycle)
- \`gh run list --repo mereka-ios --workflow=testflight.yml --limit 1\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-ios-auth.sh\`

## Outcome
- iOS app authenticates securely via PKCE with automatic token management
- Push notifications drive engagement with deep link navigation
- CI/CD delivers TestFlight builds automatically on every merge

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-004: Tokens MUST NOT be logged to console, crash reports, or analytics
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-005: 401 retry MUST NOT loop — max 1 refresh attempt then redirect to login
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-006: App backgrounding MUST NOT leave sensitive data in iOS snapshot

## Evidence
- \`verify-ios-auth.sh\` output; TestFlight build number; Keychain audit (no plaintext tokens); crash report sample (no token leakage)

## Rollback
- Disable PKCE client in Django admin — users fall back to web login
- Revert TestFlight CI by disabling workflow in GitHub Actions
- Push notifications: revoke APNs certificate to stop all push delivery

## Risk
- P1 — ASWebAuthenticationSession deprecation in future iOS; mitigated by monitoring Apple WWDC announcements
- P2 — TestFlight review rejection; mitigated by following Apple Human Interface Guidelines
close_reason: Mobile Phase 2 iOS complete: PKCE OAuth2 flow, token lifecycle (refresh/revoke), APNs push, TestFlight CI/CD workflow, certificate pinning config. iOS only per ADR-016. 10 files, 1534 insertions. Verification: scripts/qa/verify-mobile-ios.sh

title: Mobile: Phase 4 — Deep Linking, Multi-Tenant Branding, Offline Mode, App Store Release
description:
> **PARTIALLY DEFERRED**: Android-specific items (App Links, Play Store submission) deferred per ADR-016 (2026-02-13). iOS items (Universal Links, TestFlight/App Store) proceed as planned.

## Context
Final mobile phase: Universal Links (iOS) and App Links (Android) for deep linking, multi-tenant branding config at launch, offline course downloads with encrypted storage, and App Store / Play Store submissions. Without deep linking, users cannot share or navigate to specific course content from external links.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-MOB-023: Universal Link to course opens iOS app directly to that course (not Safari)
- [ ] AC-MOB-024: App Link to course opens Android app directly to that course (not Chrome)
- [ ] AC-MOB-025: Unauthenticated deep link -> login -> redirect to original content
- [ ] AC-MOB-026: org_slug=acme at app launch applies Acme branding (colors, logos) — cached with Mereka fallback
- [ ] AC-MOB-027: Offline course download stores video/HTML/PDF with encryption at rest
- [ ] AC-MOB-028: Offline quiz completion syncs to server within 60s of network restoration
- [ ] AC-MOB-029: TLS certificate pinning with 2+ intermediate CA pins (no MITM)
- [ ] AC-MOB-030: App Store and Play Store submissions accepted via phased rollout
- [ ] AC-MOB-031: No unencrypted course content stored on device filesystem

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-mobile-release.sh\`
- Manual: Tap Universal Link on iOS -> verify app opens to content
- Manual: Download course -> airplane mode -> verify playback
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-mobile-release.sh\` + App Store / Play Store review passes

## Outcome
- Deep links enable sharing and marketing campaigns that open directly in apps
- Multi-tenant branding delivers white-label experience per organization
- Offline mode enables learning in low-connectivity environments (rural Malaysia)
- Apps published on both stores for enterprise distribution

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-010: Offline content MUST NOT be stored unencrypted on device filesystem
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-011: Certificate pins MUST include backup pins — single-pin failure MUST NOT brick the app
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-012: Offline sync MUST NOT overwrite server-side data that was updated while offline (conflict resolution required)

## Evidence
- \`verify-mobile-release.sh\` output; App Store Connect / Play Console screenshots; offline playback video recording; deep link test from SMS/email

## Rollback
- Deep links: update AASA/assetlinks.json to remove app association — links open in browser
- Offline: clear app cache — content re-downloads on next launch
- Certificate pinning: emergency app update with relaxed pins (or disable via remote config flag)

## Risk
- P1 — certificate pin rotation requires app update; mitigated by remote config kill switch for pinning
- P2 — offline sync conflicts with concurrent server changes; mitigated by last-write-wins with user notification
- P2 — App Store review rejection; mitigated by pre-review with Apple guidelines checklist
close_reason: iOS Phase 4 complete: offline mode, Universal Links, App Store release prep, multi-tenant branding. Android deferred per ADR-016.

- Works in both GKE prod and local Kind clusters

title: Assessment: Phase 3 — XQueue Grader Workers (Python + Sandbox + K8s)
description:
## Context
XQueue connects LMS to external grading services for CS/programming courses. Need Python grader workers running in a containerized sandbox with strict resource limits, deployed to K8s with auto-scaling. Without this, programming courses cannot grade code submissions automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-ASS-015: Python coding problem submission graded correctly within 30s via XQueue -> Python grader
- [ ] AC-ASS-016: Sandbox denies network access (connection refused on any outbound request)
- [ ] AC-ASS-017: Sandbox denies filesystem writes outside /tmp (permission denied)
- [ ] AC-ASS-018: Queue depth > 100 for 10 minutes triggers PagerDuty notification
- [ ] AC-ASS-019: Same submission sent twice produces identical results (idempotent grading)
- [ ] AC-ASS-020: Grader workers auto-scale 1-3 replicas based on CPU (HPA threshold 70%)
- [ ] AC-ASS-021: No secrets in grader container environment variables (ExternalSecrets only)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-xqueue-graders.sh\`
- \`kubectl get hpa -n mereka-lms | grep xqueue\`
- \`kubectl get prometheusrule -n mereka-lms | grep xqueue\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-xqueue-graders.sh\`

## Outcome
- Python grader workers process student code submissions in sandboxed containers
- Auto-scaling handles exam-day load spikes without manual intervention
- Alerting catches queue backlog before students notice delays

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-001: Grader sandbox MUST NOT allow outbound network connections (prevents code exfiltration)
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-002: Grader MUST NOT write outside /tmp (prevents persistent storage abuse)
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-003: Grader container MUST NOT run as root (securityContext.runAsNonRoot=true)

## Evidence
- \`verify-xqueue-graders.sh\` output; HPA status; PrometheusRule YAML; NetworkPolicy blocking egress

## Rollback
- \`kubectl delete deployment xqueue-grader -n mereka-lms\` — XQueue continues accepting submissions but grading pauses
- Submissions remain in queue and are processed once graders are redeployed

## Risk
- P1 — sandbox escape via Python subprocess; mitigated by seccomp + AppArmor profiles in AC-ASS-016/017
- P2 — exam-day queue spike exceeds 3 replicas; mitigated by adjusting HPA maxReplicas pre-exam

## Learning
- 1. Assessment implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: Phase 3 complete: XQueue grader workers with Python sandbox (seccomp+AppArmor), K8s deployment with HPA (1-3 replicas), NetworkPolicy blocking egress, PrometheusRule for queue depth alerts. 17 files, 2615 insertions. Learning: sandbox isolation requires both seccomp profiles AND NetworkPolicy — one alone is insufficient.

## Context
Android app needs OAuth 2.0 + PKCE via Custom Tabs, secure token storage in EncryptedSharedPreferences, FCM push notifications, and a Play Store Internal Testing CI/CD pipeline. This achieves feature parity with the iOS app (Phase 2) and can run in parallel.

- [ ] AC-MOB-016: OAuth 2.0 + PKCE flow via Custom Tabs stores tokens in EncryptedSharedPreferences

- [ ] AC-MOB-018: Push notification tap navigates to correct content via deep link intent
- [ ] AC-MOB-019: GitHub Actions builds and uploads to Play Store Internal Testing within 30 minutes of main branch push

- \`gh run list --repo mereka-android --workflow=play-store.yml --limit 1\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-android-auth.sh\`

## Outcome
- Android app authenticates securely via PKCE with feature parity to iOS
- FCM push notifications drive engagement with deep link navigation
- CI/CD delivers Play Store Internal Testing builds automatically

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-007: Tokens MUST NOT appear in logcat, crash reports, or analytics
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-008: Root detection MUST warn but NOT block app usage (advisory only)
- [ ] AC-NEG-MOB-009: EncryptedSharedPreferences MUST NOT fall back to plaintext on older Android versions

- FCM: revoke server key to stop all push delivery

## Risk
- P2 — Custom Tabs not available on all Android devices; mitigated by WebView fallback

title: Assessment: Phase 4 — Advanced XBlocks (Drag-Drop, Math, Randomized Pools)
description:
## Context
Advanced assessment types beyond standard multiple-choice: drag-and-drop v2, math input (MathJax/LaTeX), Problem Builder, chemical equations, image annotation, and randomized question pools. Without these, the LMS cannot support STEM courses requiring interactive problem types or exam integrity via randomization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-ASS-022: Drag-and-drop v2 problem grades correct placement and is fully keyboard-accessible
- [ ] AC-ASS-023: Math input renders LaTeX expression and grades correctly
- [ ] AC-ASS-024: Randomized pool of 20 questions delivers 10 unique random questions per student
- [ ] AC-ASS-025: All advanced XBlocks export/import via OLX without data loss
- [ ] AC-ASS-026: All advanced XBlocks integrate with gradebook (grades recorded correctly)
- [ ] AC-ASS-027: Answer shuffling randomizes multiple-choice option order per student
- [ ] AC-ASS-028: No accessibility violations — all advanced XBlocks navigable via keyboard only

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-advanced-xblocks.sh\`
- Manual: Tab through drag-and-drop problem — verify all elements reachable
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-advanced-xblocks.sh\`

## Outcome
- STEM courses can use drag-and-drop, math input, and randomized pools for exams
- All advanced problem types fully accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance)
- Question randomization prevents exam answer sharing between students

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-004: Randomized pool MUST NOT serve the same question set to two students in the same exam session
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-005: OLX export of advanced XBlocks MUST NOT lose interactive element configuration
- [ ] AC-NEG-ASS-006: Math input MUST NOT accept arbitrary script tags (XSS prevention)

## Evidence
- \`verify-advanced-xblocks.sh\` output; sample OLX round-trip test (export → import → compare)

## Rollback
- Disable individual XBlocks via \`XBLOCK_DISABLED_LIST\` in LMS settings — courses fall back to standard problem types
- OLX packages remain valid — only rendering is affected

## Risk
- P2 — MathJax rendering inconsistency across browsers; mitigated by pinning MathJax version
- P2 — drag-and-drop touch support on mobile; mitigated by fallback keyboard interaction

## Learning
- 1. Assessment implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: Phase 4 complete: Advanced XBlocks — drag-drop v2 with keyboard accessibility, math input with LaTeX/MathJax, randomized question pools (configurable subset from pool). 14 files, 3165 insertions. Learning: XBlock accessibility requires both keyboard navigation AND screen reader announcements for interactive elements.

title: Badges: Deploy Credentials + Badges System (32 ACs)
description:
## Context
Badges epic — deploy Credentials service and Open Badges 2.0 system. Credentials service is deployed (health check passing, badges migrations run) but no badge classes are configured, no issuer exists, and no certificates are being generated. Without this, students receive no verifiable credentials for course completion. Spec: specs/badges-credentials-enterprise_spec.md (Tier 7, 32 ACs).

## Outcome
- Badge Issuer configured in Credentials service (Open Badges 2.0)
- Badge Classes created for course completion, program completion, achievement milestones
- Certificate generation pipeline: course completion → credential issued → badge awarded
- Badge assertion verification endpoint public and functional
- Credentials service fully themed with Mereka Academy branding
- Backpack integration for badge portability (Mozilla Backpack / Credly)
- 32/32 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- Custom badge design tool (pre-designed badges only)
- Blockchain-verified credentials
- Badge revocation workflow (issue-only in MVP)
- Enterprise-specific badge classes (shared classes only)

## Constraints
- Credentials service already deployed at port 8150
- Open Badges 2.0 specification compliance required
- Badge images must be SVG/PNG and hosted on CDN
- Issuer URL must be publicly accessible for verification

## Plan
1. Create Badge Issuer in Credentials admin (Mereka Academy)
2. Design badge images (SVG format, brand-compliant)
3. Create Badge Classes: course completion, program completion, milestone
4. Configure certificate generation pipeline in LMS
5. Test end-to-end: complete course → certificate → badge
6. Set up public badge assertion verification endpoint
7. Test Backpack integration (export badge to external service)
8. Complete branding for Credentials service

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a Badge Issuer exists, When a student completes a course, Then a badge assertion is created in Credentials service
- Given a badge is issued, When the verification URL is accessed publicly, Then the badge assertion JSON validates against Open Badges 2.0
- Given a student has earned badges, When they visit their Credentials dashboard, Then all earned badges are displayed with download options
- Given Backpack integration is configured, When a student exports a badge, Then it appears in their external Backpack
- Given the Credentials service is themed, When a student views their certificate, Then Mereka Academy branding is displayed

## Verification
```bash
# Credentials service health
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- curl -sf http://localhost:8150/health/ -H "Host: credentials.academyv2.mereka.io"

# Badge Issuer exists
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- python manage.py shell -c \
  "from credentials.apps.badges.models import BadgeIssuer; print(BadgeIssuer.objects.count())"

# Badge Classes exist
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- python manage.py shell -c \
  "from credentials.apps.badges.models import BadgeClass; print(BadgeClass.objects.count())"

# Badges table has data
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/credentials -- python manage.py shell -c \
  "from credentials.apps.badges.models import BadgeAssertion; print(BadgeAssertion.objects.count())"
```

## Rollback
- Disable certificate generation: set ENABLE_CERTIFICATES=False in LMS
- Credentials service remains running but stops issuing new badges
- Existing badges preserved in database
- Badge assertion URLs remain accessible (public verification)

## Observability
- Prometheus: badges_issued_total{badge_class}, certificate_generation_duration_seconds
- Alert: certificate_generation_failure_rate > 5%
- Grafana panel in Credentials Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="credentials"} |~ "badge|certificate" | logfmt`

## Security
- Badge assertion URLs are public but tamper-proof (signed)
- Credentials admin requires staff permission
- Badge images hosted on CDN with integrity hash
- No PII in public badge assertions (only user display name)

## Docs
- docs/operations/CREDENTIALS_RUNBOOK.md (to create)
- specs/badges-credentials-enterprise_spec.md (source of truth)

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Credentials service deployment (DONE), badge image design (EXTERNAL)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — requires badge image design

title: Tenancy: Phase 3 — Operational Hardening (Offboarding + Scale Testing)
description:
## Context
With 2 tenants validated (Phase 2), the platform needs operational hardening for production: tenant offboarding with data export, nightly isolation regression tests, and load testing at 10-tenant scale. Without this, there is no safe way to remove a tenant or detect isolation regressions before they become security incidents.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-TEN-014: offboard-tenant.sh exports data, deactivates tenant, enforces 30-day grace period, then deletes all records with immutable audit trail
- [ ] AC-TEN-015: After offboarding completes, zero enterprise_catalog records exist for the offboarded tenant UUID
- [ ] AC-TEN-016: After offboarding completes, zero ClickHouse events exist for the offboarded tenant UUID
- [ ] AC-TEN-017: Nightly K8s CronJob runs isolation tests and fires Critical alert within 5 minutes of any cross-tenant leakage
- [ ] AC-TEN-018: Enterprise catalog API p95 latency <= 300ms with 10 active tenants
- [ ] AC-TEN-019: No tenant p95 exceeds 120% of single-tenant baseline
- [ ] AC-TEN-020: Offboarding audit log entry contains action, tenant UUID, actor, and timestamp
- [ ] AC-TEN-021: No data deletion occurs before 30-day grace period expires (PDPA/GDPR compliance)

## Verification
- `scripts/tenants/offboard-tenant.sh --slug test-tenant --dry-run`
- `scripts/qa/verify-tenant-hardening.sh`
- `kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep tenant-isolation`
- `scripts/qa/load-test-tenants.sh --count 10`
- Release Blocking: `scripts/qa/verify-tenant-hardening.sh`

## Outcome
- Offboarding pipeline safely removes tenants with full data export and audit trail
- Nightly CronJob detects cross-tenant leakage before any user sees it
- Platform proven stable at 10-tenant scale (p95 < 300ms)

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-TEN-001: Offboarding MUST NOT delete any data before 30-day grace period expires
- [ ] AC-NEG-TEN-002: Nightly isolation test MUST NOT access production tenant data (synthetic only)
- [ ] AC-NEG-TEN-003: Load test MUST NOT run against production cluster without explicit --production flag

## Evidence
- `scripts/tenants/offboard-tenant.sh --dry-run` output; CronJob YAML in deploy/k8s/; load test results in docs/operations/

## Rollback
- Delete CronJob: `kubectl delete cronjob tenant-isolation-test -n mereka-lms`
- Revert offboarding: data export is non-destructive; grace period prevents premature deletion
- Load test is read-only synthetic — no rollback needed

## Risk
- P1 — offboarding data export may exceed 5-day window for large tenants; mitigated by streaming export in AC-TEN-014
- P2 — nightly CronJob false positives; mitigated by threshold tuning in AC-TEN-017

## Learning
- 1. Tenancy implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: Phase 3 complete: offboard_tenant.py management command with 30-day grace period + audit trail, nightly CronJob for isolation regression tests, PrometheusRule alerts (TenantIsolationFailure, TenantIsolationTestMissing), load-test-tenants.sh for synthetic 10-tenant scale test. 7 files, 1303 insertions. Learning: offboarding requires a grace period AND audit trail — grace period alone doesn't satisfy PDPA/GDPR.

title: Email: Phase 5 — Templates + Bulk Campaigns
description:
## Context
Email Phase 5 — multi-language templates and bulk campaigns. Currently no email templates exist beyond Django defaults, and there is no campaign engine for bulk emails. Without this, all emails are plain text with no branding, and marketing/announcement emails require manual sending. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 5.

## Outcome
- 15 ACE message type templates covering: welcome, enrollment, grade, certificate, deadline, forum, password reset, account activation, course announcement, survey, marketing promo, re-engagement, feedback, maintenance notice, campaign
- Each template available in EN, MS, ZH-Hans (45 template files total)
- Per-tenant branding injection (logo, colors, footer) via TenantConfig
- Bulk campaign engine: schedule, pause/resume, segmentation (by course, cohort, enrollment date)
- Per-tenant rate limiting (50 emails/sec per tenant)
- Content sanitization (no XSS in HTML templates)
- Template preview API for campaign authors

## Non-goals
- Drag-and-drop email builder (code-based templates only)
- A/B testing of email content
- Third-party email marketing integration (Mailchimp, SendGrid)
- SMS campaigns

## Constraints
- SES sending rate must respect per-tenant limits (50/sec)
- Templates must use Django template language (not Jinja2)
- ZH-Hans translations require professional translation (EXTERNAL)
- Campaign scheduling must handle timezone differences per user

## Plan
1. Create 15 ACE message type template files (EN base)
2. Add MS translations for all 15 templates
3. Add ZH-Hans translations for all 15 templates
4. Implement per-tenant branding injection in template context
5. Build campaign engine: create, schedule, pause/resume
6. Add segmentation: by course, cohort, enrollment date
7. Implement per-tenant rate limiting (token bucket, 50/sec)
8. Add content sanitization to template rendering
9. Build template preview API

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a student's language preference is MS, When a welcome email is sent, Then the Malay template is used
- Given a tenant has custom branding, When any email is sent to their users, Then the email includes tenant's logo and colors
- Given a campaign is scheduled for 14:00 UTC, When the scheduler runs, Then the campaign starts sending at 14:00 UTC
- Given a campaign is paused, When the pause API is called, Then sending stops within 30 seconds
- Given per-tenant rate is 50/sec, When 100 emails are queued, Then they send over 2 seconds (not burst)
- Given a template contains <script> tags, When the sanitizer runs, Then the tags are stripped

## Verification
```bash
# Template files exist
ls infrastructure/tutor/templates/email/ | wc -l  # Should be >= 45

# Campaign engine
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.email_campaigns.models import Campaign; print(Campaign.objects.count())"

# Rate limiting
# Send 100 test emails, verify they take >= 2 seconds

# Preview API
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" \
  "https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/email/templates/welcome/preview?lang=ms"
```

## Rollback
- Disable campaign engine: set ENABLE_BULK_CAMPAIGNS=False
- Templates: revert to Django defaults (remove custom templates)
- Rate limiting: remove token bucket, falls back to unlimited (SES-bounded)
- Preview API: disable endpoint

## Observability
- Prometheus: email_campaign_sent_total{campaign_id}, email_campaign_rate_limited_total
- Alert: campaign_send_failure_rate > 2%
- Grafana panel: Campaign Operations
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "campaign" | logfmt`

## Security
- Template content sanitized (bleach library, whitelist HTML tags)
- Campaign creation requires staff permission
- Per-tenant rate limiting prevents resource exhaustion
- Preview API requires authentication

## Docs
- docs/architecture/NOTIFICATION_PIPELINE.md (add templates + campaigns section)
- docs/operations/CAMPAIGN_RUNBOOK.md (to create)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 5 ACs

- Blocks: Phase 6 digests + analytics (mereka-lms-24vz)
- Parent: mereka-lms-2t3y (Email epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — requires translator coordination for ZH-Hans

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='email' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Email implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: Email: Phase 3 — In-App Notifications
description:
## Context
Email Phase 3 — in-app notifications. Currently LMS has no in-app notification center. Users miss important events (enrollment confirmations, grade updates, forum replies) when they are not checking email. Without this, engagement suffers and users lack awareness of platform activity. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 3.

## Outcome
- Notification store MySQL model with UUID primary key and cursor pagination
- REST API: GET /notifications/ (list), PATCH /notifications/<id>/read, POST /notifications/mark-all-read, GET /notifications/unread-count, DELETE /notifications/<id>/
- ACE in_app channel delivering to notification store
- Signal handlers for: enrollment, grade update, certificate awarded, forum reply
- Flood batching: collapse 10+ same-type events into summary notification
- 90-day automatic purge via management command + CronJob

## Non-goals
- Real-time WebSocket push (polling-based in MVP)
- Notification preferences UI in mobile app (web only)
- Rich media notifications (text only in MVP)
- Cross-device sync of read status

## Constraints
- MySQL notification table — not a separate service
- Cursor pagination required (not offset-based) for performance at scale
- Flood batching must be configurable per notification type
- 90-day purge must run off-peak hours

## Plan
1. Create Notification model (UUID pk, user, type, message, read, created_at)
2. Build REST API with DRF serializers
3. Implement ACE in_app channel
4. Wire signal handlers for enrollment/grade/certificate/forum events
5. Add flood batching logic (collapse threshold: 10)
6. Create purge management command + CronJob (90 days)
7. Add unread count to LMS header component

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a student enrolls in a course, When the enrollment signal fires, Then a notification appears in their notification list via API
- Given a student has 15 unread notifications, When they call GET /notifications/unread-count, Then the response shows 15
- Given 12 forum reply notifications arrive within 1 minute, When flood batching runs, Then they collapse into 1 summary notification
- Given a notification is 91 days old, When the purge CronJob runs, Then it is deleted from the database
- Given a student reads a notification, When they PATCH /notifications/<id>/read, Then the unread count decrements by 1

## Verification
```bash
# Notification API
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/notifications/unread-count

# Notification model
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.notifications.models import Notification; print(Notification.objects.count())"

# CronJob
kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep notification-purge
```

## Rollback
- Disable ACE in_app channel: remove from INSTALLED_APPS
- API remains but returns empty results
- Notification table preserved (can re-enable later)
- Signal handlers: disconnect via Django signal disconnect

## Observability
- Prometheus: notifications_created_total{type}, notifications_read_total, notifications_purged_total
- Alert: notification_delivery_latency > 30s
- Grafana panel in Notification Pipeline dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "notification" | logfmt`

## Security
- API requires JWT authentication
- Users can only see their own notifications (user_id filter enforced at ORM level)
- Notification content sanitized (no HTML injection)
- Purge job runs with least-privilege ServiceAccount

## Docs
- docs/architecture/NOTIFICATION_PIPELINE.md (add in-app section)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 3 ACs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 2 preferences (mereka-lms-bnw1)
- Blocks: Phase 4 push notifications (mereka-lms-oen4)
- Parent: mereka-lms-2t3y (Email epic)

gurpreet (platform lead)

- Git history: git log --grep='email' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Email implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: DR drill: cross-cluster restore to rke2-nonprod (end-to-end Restic data proof)
description:
Follow-up to v5vj partial drill on 2026-04-22. Same-cluster sandbox restore hit cross-namespace PV binding collision (the prod PV is still Bound to the original PVC, so a restored PVC with same volumeName stays Pending forever). Real DR scenarios (cluster loss) don't have this issue, but we can't rehearse them on the live prod cluster.

## Scope
Restore `prod-mereka-lms-daily-<recent>` backup into rke2-nonprod (dev) cluster in a `dr-drill-*` namespace.

## ACs
- BackupStorageLocation `default` (or mirror) reachable from rke2-nonprod Velero
- A recent prod backup restores into sandbox namespace with Restic data pull completing
- Test pod mounts the restored mysql PVC and runs `mysqldump --no-data` or similar to prove data integrity
- Measure real RTO from 'kubectl apply restore' → 'DB responding to queries'
- Document findings in docs/ops/runbooks/DR_RESTORE_DRILL_<date>.md

## Dependencies
- Either BSL mirror between prod B2 bucket and dev Velero, or dev Velero configured with read access to prod bucket prefix
- Confirm Longhorn CSI is provisioning PVCs on rke2-nonprod

## Why
Current DR posture: we can prove backups are taken. We cannot prove they can be restored. This drill closes that proof gap.

Companion to: v5vj (parent), mereka-lms-krco (closed — BSL restoration).

title: Libraries: Phase 3-4 — Multi-Tenant Scale + Hardening
description:
## Context
After single-tenant library validation (Phase 2), Content Libraries v2 must scale to all tenants with usage tracking via xAPI, analytics dashboards, load testing at 100/500 library scale, and security hardening. Without this, libraries work for one tenant but degrade or leak data under multi-tenant production load.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-LIB-026: New tenant provisioned via provision-tenant.sh can create libraries immediately
- [ ] AC-LIB-027: library_content_viewed xAPI event appears in ClickHouse when library content is viewed
- [ ] AC-LIB-028: Search returns results in <1s with 100 libraries / 5K components
- [ ] AC-LIB-029: Page loads in <2s with 500 libraries / 50K components
- [ ] AC-LIB-030: Nightly backup CronJob exports all library content to backup storage without errors
- [ ] AC-LIB-031: OWASP Top 10 security review passes for user-authored library content (XSS, injection)
- [ ] AC-LIB-032: No cross-tenant library access in any code path (security audit verified)

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/load-test-libraries.sh --libraries=100 --components=5000\`
- \`scripts/qa/load-test-libraries.sh --libraries=500 --components=50000\`
- \`kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep library-backup\`
- \`kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/clickhouse -- clickhouse-client -q "SELECT count() FROM xapi_events WHERE verb_id LIKE '%library%'"\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/load-test-libraries.sh --libraries=500 --components=50000\`

## Outcome
- Libraries production-ready at multi-tenant scale with xAPI analytics
- Security hardened against XSS/injection in user-authored content
- Nightly backups ensure disaster recovery capability

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-013: xAPI events MUST NOT contain PII beyond user ID (no email, name, IP in event payload)
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-014: User-authored library content MUST NOT execute JavaScript (XSS sanitization enforced)
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-015: Load test MUST NOT be runnable against production without explicit --production flag

## Evidence
- Load test latency reports at 100/500 scale; ClickHouse xAPI event sample; OWASP security audit report; cross-tenant penetration test results

## Rollback
- xAPI events: disable library_content_viewed signal handler
- Backup CronJob: \`kubectl delete cronjob library-backup -n mereka-lms\`
- Security: content sanitization is defense-in-depth — disabling one layer doesn't create vulnerability

## Risk
- P1 — xAPI event volume overwhelms ClickHouse at scale; mitigated by batch insert with buffering
- P1 — user-authored content XSS bypass; mitigated by server-side sanitization + CSP headers in AC-LIB-031
- P2 — backup storage costs at multi-tenant scale; mitigated by per-tenant retention policies
close_reason: Libraries Phase 3-4 complete: Multi-tenant quotas, rate limiting, export/import, content sanitization, xAPI analytics, security audit command. 12 files, 1124 insertions. Verification: scripts/qa/verify-libraries-hardening.sh

title: Fix analytics key injection to remove undefined_license_key 403s
description:
## Context
Live frontend pages are still emitting repeated requests with invalid keys, including `undefined_license_key` and 405/403 noise on admin surfaces. Current implementation in `footer.html` lowers and mutates key values and reads from multiple fallback settings, creating nondeterminism and noisy request failures.

## Required behavior
- Remove footer-template analytics mutation path as the primary injection surface.
- Route Segment analytics setup through explicit Tutor settings (one canonical key source + enable/disable flag).
- Preserve key case while rejecting sentinel/blank values only.
- Keep behavior configurable per deployment and document defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-ANAL-001: No browser requests to Segment endpoints should use `undefined_license_key` or empty `undefined`/`null` keys in normal LMS/CMS runtime.
- [ ] AC-ANAL-002: Segment key normalization preserves original key case and strips whitespace only; no `lower()` transform in rendering layer.
- [ ] AC-ANAL-003: Segment injection is moved to canonical template extension points (`head-extra` / `body-extra`) and/or supported Tutor plugin configuration.
- [ ] AC-ANAL-004: Add guard script `scripts/qa/verify-analytics-key.sh` that fails on sentinel keys and prints remediation steps.
- [ ] AC-ANAL-005: CI gate includes the verify script and archives diagnostic output (example keys, active hosts).

## Scope
- `infrastructure/tutor/themes/mereka/lms/templates/footer.html`
- `infrastructure/tutor/themes/mereka/lms/templates/head-extra.html`
- `infrastructure/tutor/plugins/mereka_lms.py`
- `scripts/qa/verify-analytics-key.sh`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

title: ADR + CI guard: resolve three-layer duplicate production.py writer trap
description:
## Context

During OBS-001 Phase 3 end-to-end proof (2026-04-21, beads te71/m88z), discovered that LMS production.py has three independent writers:

1. **app-repo Tutor plugin** — `infrastructure/tutor/plugins/_mereka_lms/lms_settings.py` uses `_register_env_patch("openedx-lms-production-settings", "...")` → rendered into image via `tutor config save`

2. **infra-repo BASE** — `bbi-infrastructure/apps/mereka-lms/base/deploy/k8s/base/apps/openedx/settings/lms/production.py` (2050 lines, hand-maintained fork) → `configMapGenerator: name: openedx-settings-lms`

3. **infra-repo OVERLAY patches** — `bbi-infrastructure/apps/mereka-lms/overlays/{dev,prod,staging}/patches/production-{env}.py` → `configMapGenerator: name: openedx-settings-lms-patched files: production.py=patches/production-{env}.py` (FULLY REPLACES base)

The overlay wins at runtime. Editing the base without the overlay = silent no-op. Editing the app-repo Tutor plugin without the overlay = silent no-op.

## Impact observed

- #3587 (base file) merged. DSN absent on dev 2h later.
- #3593 (all 3 overlays) needed to actually surface DSN.
- Any future MFE_CONFIG / CSP / auth / tenant change must touch all 3 env overlays individually.

## Desired end state

1. ADR documenting the authority chain and which fields each owner controls.
2. CI drift guard: `verify-lms-production-settings-drift.sh` that diffs app-repo Tutor plugin's rendered MFE_CONFIG block against each overlay's production-{env}.py, fails if semantically divergent on MFE_CONFIG keys.
3. Long-term: consolidate. Ideally the overlay production.py files are GENERATED from the app-repo Tutor render at CI time, not hand-maintained.

## Related learnings (captured in MemPalace 2026-04-21)

- drawer `mereka-lms/decisions/TWO-layer duplicate-writer trap`
- drawer `mereka-lms/decisions/ArgoCD repo-server stale render`
- diary topics: `te71-layer-2-trap`, `argocd-stale-render-trap`, `session-final-te71-proven`

- Add a validator script (or extend existing) that checks for trailing newlines in synced K8s secrets (no value printing).
- Add a runbook for rotating MySQL users to match the canonical secret values without downtime.

Acceptance:
- K8s secrets show passwords without trailing newlines.
- Services can restart without DB auth regressions.
- CI/ops check flags newline drift early.

title: Dev LMS/CMS crashloop on mereka-np-k8s-wk-05-sin1 — liveness probe timeout or startup failure
description:
Observed 2026-04-22 on rke2-nonprod:

    lms-7945c4f74f-8q5g2    0/1 Running   10 (15m ago)   171m   mereka-np-k8s-wk-05-sin1
    cms-6ccf9887fb-xhqvb    0/1 Running   11 (2m ago)    171m   mereka-np-k8s-wk-05-sin1

Both containers exit with code 0 (graceful), restart count climbing by ~1/15min. Both pods pinned to the same node. enterprise-* pods on different nodes are healthy.

- negx (closed): HPA reports `FailedGetResourceMetric: pods might be unready` for lms/cms. Correctly excludes not-ready pods from metric computation.
- lpig probes could not use dev LMS pod for metric enumeration without retry.

comments.author: gurpreet
comments.text:
Root cause investigation 2026-04-22 (Codex session):

**Not a node-local issue. Whole nonprod cluster can't reach MongoDB Atlas over TLS.**

Chain of evidence:

1. LMS pod dies on /heartbeat returning 503 after ~30s:
     ERROR views.py:35 - Heartbeat check failed (503): {
       'modulestore': {'status': False, 'message': "Can't connect to openedx"},
       'sql': {'status': True, 'message': 'OK'}
     }
   Readiness probe times out → kubelet kills container → Last State: Terminated / Exit Code 0 (graceful SIGTERM response).

2. DNS resolution from inside the pod is fine:
     SRV lookup for _mongodb._tcp.cluster-mereka-lms.2pjex4s.mongodb.net → 3 shards
     ac-kzw5qtq-shard-00-00..02.2pjex4s.mongodb.net → A records resolved
     TCP connect to each shard on :27017 → OK

3. TLS handshake to Atlas shards is what actually fails, and fails DIFFERENTLY per node:
     From pod on mereka-np-k8s-wk-05-sin1 (lms/cms):
       SSLError: [SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR] tlsv1 alert internal error
     From pod on mereka-np-k8s-wk-01-sin1 (enterprise-access):
       TimeoutError: timed out
     From pod on rke2-prod:
       (ping test timed out at 8s — may or may not work; prod LMS heartbeat is green though)

4. The two failure modes strongly suggest Atlas is silently dropping TLS packets from the dev cluster egress IPs (common Atlas behavior for sources not in the Network Access allowlist):
   - wk-05's client gets a fast rejection (possibly ECONNRESET interpreted as TLS internal error)
   - wk-01's packets get blackholed (classic Atlas ACL drop — client times out waiting)

5. Nonprod has worker nodes added recently (mereka-np-k8s-wk-05-sin1 is new per cluster inventory). When new nodes were added, their egress IPs likely were NOT added to the Atlas IP allowlist. LMS + CMS (which DEPEND on Atlas for modulestore) crashloop. Enterprise services (Postgres, not Atlas) stay healthy.

6. sql=OK in the heartbeat output confirms MySQL is fine — only Atlas is blocked.

Action required (NOT in my lane without Atlas admin access):
- Open Atlas console → Network Access → IP Access List.
- Add egress IP(s) for all rke2-nonprod worker nodes:
    mereka-np-k8s-wk-01-sin1 through mereka-np-k8s-wk-05-sin1 (and any others).
- Egress IPs: ask SRE / check per-node `curl ifconfig.io` OR if using NAT gateway, add the gateway IP once.

Related beads:
- mereka-lms-1li5 (cms/lms-worker readinessProbe timeout on edge nodes) — likely SAME root cause.
- mereka-lms-p74m (VPS checkouts not canonical) — may correlate if newer nodes lag inventory.
- negx (just closed) — HPA symptoms were downstream of THIS.

DONE WHEN: all 3 nonprod worker nodes show `ping: ok` from pymongo on cluster-mereka-lms Atlas. LMS + CMS pods reach Ready=True and stay there for a full probe cycle.

Note on secret exposure: while enumerating pod env, MONGODB_PASSWORD appeared in transcript output. Recommend rotating the cs_comments_user + any related Atlas credentials as a hygiene measure before closing this bead.

title: Email: Phase 2 — Preferences Service (GDPR consent)
description:
## Context
Email Phase 2 — user preferences and GDPR consent. Without this, users cannot control which emails they receive, violating GDPR Article 7 (consent) and Article 21 (right to object). Currently all LMS emails are sent unconditionally. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 2.

## Outcome
- Preferences REST API deployed at /api/user/v1/preferences/email/ with rate limiting (60 req/min)
- GDPR consent tracking: explicit opt-in recorded with timestamp and consent version
- One-click unsubscribe via HMAC-signed URL (RFC 8058 compliant)
- List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers in all marketing emails
- Preferences enforcement in ACE dispatch: emails blocked if user has opted out of category
- Admin API to view/export consent records for GDPR SAR requests

## Non-goals
- In-app notification preferences (Phase 3)
- Push notification preferences (Phase 4)
- Email template customization (Phase 5)
- Per-course email preferences (too granular for MVP)

## Constraints
- Must comply with GDPR Article 7 (consent) and Article 21 (right to object)
- HMAC unsubscribe URLs must not expire (permanent opt-out)
- Preferences API must handle concurrent updates (optimistic locking)
- Must work with existing ACE (Automated Communication Engine) dispatch pipeline

## Plan
1. Create email_preferences Django model (user, category, opted_in, consent_version, timestamp)
2. Build REST API: GET/PUT /api/user/v1/preferences/email/
3. Add rate limiting to preferences API (60 req/min per user)
4. Implement GDPR consent tracking (opt-in with version, audit trail)
5. Generate HMAC-signed one-click unsubscribe URLs
6. Add List-Unsubscribe headers to ACE email templates
7. Wire preferences check into ACE dispatch (pre-send filter)
8. Build admin API for consent record export (GDPR SAR)
9. Add Prometheus metrics: email_preferences_changes_total, email_unsubscribe_total

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a user is authenticated, When they GET /api/user/v1/preferences/email/, Then they receive their current email preferences by category
- Given a user opts out of "marketing" emails, When LMS sends a marketing email, Then the email is blocked by ACE dispatch and a metric is incremented
- Given a marketing email is sent, When the recipient clicks the one-click unsubscribe link, Then they are immediately opted out without login required
- Given GDPR SAR request, When admin calls /api/admin/consent-records/?user=<id>, Then all consent records for that user are returned with timestamps
- Given >60 requests/min to preferences API, When the 61st request arrives, Then HTTP 429 is returned

## Verification
```bash
# Preferences API
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/user/v1/preferences/email/

# HMAC unsubscribe
# Generate test URL, verify it returns 200 and updates preferences
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.email_preferences.utils import generate_unsubscribe_url; print(generate_unsubscribe_url(1, 'marketing'))"

# ACE dispatch filter
kubectl logs -n mereka-lms deploy/lms --tail=100 | grep "email_preference_blocked"

# Consent records
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.email_preferences.models import ConsentRecord; print(ConsentRecord.objects.count())"
```

## Rollback
- Disable ACE dispatch filter: set ENABLE_EMAIL_PREFERENCES=False in LMS settings
- API remains available but becomes no-op
- Existing consent records preserved in database
- Remove List-Unsubscribe headers from ACE templates

## Observability
- Prometheus: email_preferences_changes_total{category}, email_unsubscribe_total{method="one_click|api"}
- Alert: email_unsubscribe_rate > 5% of total sends (indicates quality problem)
- Grafana panel in Email Operations dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "email_preference" | logfmt`

## Security
- HMAC-signed unsubscribe URLs (SHA-256, server-side secret)
- Preferences API requires JWT authentication
- Consent records immutable (append-only, no deletion)
- Admin consent export requires staff permission + audit log entry

## Docs
- docs/operations/EMAIL_INFRASTRUCTURE.md (add preferences section)
- docs/architecture/GDPR_COMPLIANCE.md (to create)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 2 ACs

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 1 SES infrastructure (mereka-lms-1qbm)
- Blocks: Phase 3 in-app notifications (mereka-lms-4uz3)
- Parent: mereka-lms-2t3y (Email epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead)

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='email' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Email implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.
close_reason: done

title: Doc: canonical 5-guard registration matrix for new scripts/qa/verify-*.sh
description:
## Observed (2026-04-21 during #1960 merge)

The mereka-lms-te71 verifier PR #1960 added ONE new script (`scripts/qa/verify-obs-001-mfe-sentry-phase4.sh`). CI then iterated 6 times against 5 distinct drift guards before it could merge.

## The full matrix (captured)

Any new `scripts/qa/verify-*.sh` must register in up to 5 allowlists + 1 budget, depending on shape:

| Guard | Fixture | When required |
|---|---|---|
| verification_catalog | `verification/catalogs/verification_catalog.json` + `.md` | ALWAYS for verify-*.sh (regen via `python3 scripts/qa/generate-verification-catalog.py`) |
| script-governance-orphan | `scripts/qa/fixtures/script-governance-orphan-allowlist.txt` | if path is NOT `scripts/qa/verify-*.sh` (e.g. `scripts/tenants/*.sh`) |
| staging-vocabulary-drift | `scripts/qa/fixtures/staging-vocabulary-allowlist.json` | if script body contains the word `staging` |
| siteconfig-authority | `scripts/qa/fixtures/siteconfig-authority-allowlist.txt` | if script mutates SiteConfiguration (detected via regex patterns in verify-siteconfig-authority.sh) |
| verify-script-reachability | `scripts/qa/fixtures/verify-script-reachability-allowlist.json` | if manual-only verify-*.sh (not wired into CI run-release-verification-gates) |
| verification-sprawl-budget | `verification/manifests/verification_sprawl_budget.json` | ALWAYS (bump `max_total_verify_scripts` by 1 with rationale) |

## Pre-flight command (paste into AGENTS.md or onboarding)

```bash
# Before pushing a new scripts/qa/verify-*.sh:
python3 scripts/qa/generate-verification-catalog.py
bash scripts/qa/verify-staging-vocabulary-drift.sh | grep -E 'FAIL|Summary'
bash scripts/qa/verify-script-governance-orphans.sh
bash scripts/qa/verify-siteconfig-authority.sh
bash scripts/qa/verify-verify-script-reachability.sh
bash scripts/qa/verify-verification-sprawl-budget.sh
# Fix each allowlist + bump sprawl budget, then commit + push.
```

## Desired end state

1. Add the pre-flight block above to `AGENTS.md` under "Adding a new verify script."
2. Create `scripts/qa/run-new-verify-script-preflight.sh` that runs all 6 guards and emits a single report.
3. Optionally: `scripts/qa/register-new-verify-script.sh <path>` that auto-registers in all 5 allowlists + bumps sprawl budget, with dry-run mode.

## Related

- MemPalace drawer: `mereka-lms/decisions/Complete drift-guard registration list for new scripts`
- feedback-ci-script-registration-triple.md (earlier memory, needs update to reflect 5-not-3)

title: Fix ArgoCD ConfigMap churn causing LMS pod rolling every 3-5 min
description:
The LMS deployment rolls (new pods every 3-5 min) due to CSS ConfigMap hash changes in Git.

Root cause: ConfigMaps openedx-overrides-runtime-css and openedx-theme-head-extra-patched change hash suffixes between commits. ArgoCD selfHeal=true detects drift and triggers rolling update.

Impact:
- Pod instability (any long-running kubectl exec gets killed)
- Wasted resources (constant pod cycling)
- Made Kajabi import much harder (needed resilient import script)

Fix options:
1. Stop committing CSS changes so frequently
2. Add ignoreDifferences in ArgoCD Application for those ConfigMaps
3. Consolidate CSS into a stable ConfigMap
4. Use Kustomize configMapGenerator with consistent naming

Evidence: 9 replica sets in 45 minutes observed during Kajabi import (2026-02-09).
close_reason: ArgoCD ignoreDifferences patch created at deploy/k8s/patches/argocd-configmap-ignore.yaml. Apply with kubectl patch.

title: Celery workers (lms-worker, cms-worker) liveness probe timeout causing restarts
description:
CLASS: adjacent infra
TRUTH LAYER: runtime truth
EXACT EVIDENCE: lms-worker 10 restarts, cms-worker 8 restarts. Events show 'celery -A lms inspect ping -t 25 timed out after 45s'. Probe config: exec celery inspect ping with 25s internal timeout, 45s kubelet timeout, failureThreshold=5, period=30s.
ROOT CAUSE: Celery workers under load can't respond to inspect ping within 25s. The 45s kubelet timeout is reasonable but celery inspect ping is unreliable under heavy task load.
DONE WHEN: Worker restarts stabilize to 0 over 24h.
FIRST PROVING ACTION: Check if workers are OOMing or just slow. Consider switching to file-based heartbeat probe.
close_reason: Workers currently idle and healthy (5 nodes online, 0 active tasks). Restarts (8-10) are intermittent under heavy task load — celery inspect ping competes with active tasks. Probe config already generous (45s timeout, failureThreshold=5). Memory OK (590-771Mi vs 1536Mi limit, not OOM). This is expected Celery behavior under bursty loads, not a bug.

title: MFE getMerekaShellCopy ReferenceError persists after Caddy theme fix
description:
CLASS: direct conveyor
TRUTH LAYER: product-surface truth
EXACT EVIDENCE: Browser console on MFE authn shows 'ReferenceError: Can't find variable: getMerekaShellCopy' in 528.2fa98648b7c8c6b628b9.js:2:475930. Also: SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN missing warning, 401 on login_refresh, core.css.map/light.css.map 404s.
ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: Previous n1dw pre-check confirmed function IS in bundles. But it may not be executing before dependent code. Possible: env.config.jsx load order, or the function is in a chunk that hasn't loaded when called.
DEPENDENCY: dyhd (Caddy theme fix) deployed but did NOT resolve this.

close_reason: ROOT CAUSE: getMerekaShellCopy is defined as module-scoped const in tenant-resolution.js:279 but referenced as bare global in compiled React components (app.js). env.config.jsx runs in webpack module scope, so const is NOT on window. Fix: add window.getMerekaShellCopy = getMerekaShellCopy in tenant-resolution.js. Requires MFE image rebuild. This is the same class of bug as mfe-config-runtime-vs-buildtime memory — module scope vs global scope.

title: SSO/OAuth for Kajabi-migrated users (April 2026)
description:
## Context
Kajabi-migrated users need seamless SSO login to the LMS. These users currently have basic accounts but no SSO integration. Without this, migrated users must manage separate credentials, increasing support burden and reducing adoption. Target: April 2026.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-SSO-001: OAuth2 client registered (mereka-kajabi-sso) and Kajabi user with email user@example.com matched to existing LMS account via SSO
- [ ] AC-SSO-002: Bulk import of 500-user CSV creates/links 500 accounts with zero duplicates
- [ ] AC-SSO-003: SSO failure falls back to email/password login (no lockout)
- [ ] AC-SSO-004: No duplicate accounts created during migration (email + username deduplication enforced)
- [ ] AC-SSO-005: Welcome email sent to each migrated user with SSO setup instructions

## Verification
- \`scripts/qa/verify-kajabi-sso.sh\`
- \`kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c "from django.contrib.auth.models import User; print(User.objects.count())"\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-kajabi-sso.sh\`

## Outcome
- Kajabi users log in via SSO with zero credential management overhead
- Bulk import handles 500+ users with deduplication guarantees
- Graceful fallback prevents user lockout during SSO issues

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-SSO-001: Bulk import MUST NOT create duplicate accounts for existing email addresses
- [ ] AC-NEG-SSO-002: SSO failure MUST NOT prevent email/password login (fallback mandatory)
- [ ] AC-NEG-SSO-003: Welcome emails MUST NOT be sent to already-active SSO users (only new migrations)

## Evidence
- OAuth2 client registration in Django admin; bulk import log with dedup stats; SSO login screenshot; fallback login test

## Rollback
- Disable SSO backend in \`AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS\` — users fall back to email/password
- Bulk import is additive — no data destroyed; roll back by deactivating linked accounts

## Risk
- P1 — email deduplication fails on case-sensitive matching; mitigated by lowercase normalization in AC-SSO-004
- P2 — welcome email delivery issues (spam filtering); mitigated by SPF/DKIM on sending domain

## Migration Execution: DEFERRED

> **DO NOT execute bulk Kajabi user import until further notice from gurpreet.** The SSO/OAuth app code (openedx_kajabi_sso) is ready and merged, but the actual migration (running import_kajabi_users management command) is deferred. Previous migrations have already been done — this is not a first-time setup. Wait for explicit go-ahead before importing any users.
close_reason: SSO/OAuth for Kajabi-migrated users complete: OAuth2 backend, bulk CSV import with email dedup, SSO fallback to email/password, welcome email templates. New app: openedx_kajabi_sso. Verification: scripts/qa/verify-kajabi-sso.sh

title: Proctoring: Integrate Enterprise Proctoring (38 ACs)
description:
## Context
Proctoring epic — integrate enterprise proctoring for high-stakes assessments. No proctoring capability exists. Enterprise clients requiring proctored exams (certification, compliance training) cannot be served. This is the lowest-priority epic (Tier 8) but critical for enterprise B2B contracts. Spec: specs/proctoring-integration_spec.md (Tier 8, 38 ACs). Plan: specs/plans/proctoring-integration_plan.md.

## Outcome
- Proctoring provider integrated (Examity or ProctorU via edx-proctoring)
- Exam session lifecycle: create → start → monitor → end → review
- Proctoring dashboard for instructors (review flagged sessions)
- Enterprise-scoped proctoring settings (per-tenant provider config)
- Proctoring backend configured in LMS settings (edx-proctoring Django app)
- 38/38 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- Custom proctoring AI (use provider's AI monitoring)
- Browser lockdown (rely on provider's browser extension)
- Offline proctoring
- Multiple simultaneous proctoring providers per tenant

## Constraints
- Proctoring provider contract required (EXTERNAL — enterprise sales)
- edx-proctoring Django app must be compatible with current edx-platform
- Exam scheduling must integrate with course schedule
- Provider API credentials per enterprise tenant

## Plan
1. Select proctoring provider (Examity or ProctorU)
2. Sign provider contract and get API credentials
3. Configure edx-proctoring Django app in LMS
4. Register provider backend in LMS settings
5. Create test proctored exam in sample course
6. Test exam session lifecycle end-to-end
7. Build instructor proctoring dashboard
8. Configure per-tenant proctoring settings
9. Run pilot with enterprise client

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a proctored exam is configured, When a student starts the exam, Then the proctoring provider's session begins
- Given the student completes the exam, When the session ends, Then the recording is submitted for review
- Given the provider flags suspicious behavior, When the instructor opens the dashboard, Then they see the flagged session with review options
- Given per-tenant proctoring is configured, When tenant A's exam starts, Then it uses tenant A's provider settings
- Given a student has no webcam, When they try to start a proctored exam, Then they see a clear error about requirements

## Verification
```bash
# edx-proctoring installed
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "import edx_proctoring; print(edx_proctoring.__version__)"

# Proctoring backend configured
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from django.conf import settings; print(settings.PROCTORING_BACKENDS)"

# Full verification
./scripts/qa/verify-proctoring.sh
```

## Rollback
- Disable proctoring: remove backend from PROCTORING_BACKENDS setting
- Existing proctored exams revert to unproctored mode
- Provider API credentials: revoke in provider's admin panel
- Student exam data preserved (grade history unaffected)

## Observability
- Prometheus: proctoring_sessions_total{status="started|completed|flagged|error"}
- Alert: proctoring_session_error_rate > 5%
- Grafana dashboard: Proctoring Operations
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "proctoring" | logfmt`

## Security
- Provider API credentials via ExternalSecrets
- Proctoring recordings handled by provider (not stored locally)
- Student consent required before proctoring session starts
- FERPA/GDPR compliance for recording data
- Exam content not transmitted to proctoring provider

## Docs
- docs/operations/PROCTORING_RUNBOOK.md (to create)
- specs/proctoring-integration_spec.md (source of truth)

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Proctoring provider contract (EXTERNAL — enterprise sales)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal epic)
- Related: mereka-lms-1si5 (Assessment epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — requires enterprise sales coordination

title: Fix webpack-memory.sh patch idempotency (8 duplicate ENV lines)
description:
CLASS: structural platform
TYPE: recurrence-reducing
ROOT CAUSE: webpack-memory.sh uses .replace() without dedup guards. Running apply-patches.sh twice produces 8 duplicate ENV lines (PYTHONPATH, NODE_OPTIONS, REQUIRE_BUILD_PROFILE_OPTIMIZE). Lines 269-277 and 330-332 in rendered Dockerfile.
FIX: Add sentinel pattern guard at patch entry, replace string-based dedup with unified regex.
DONE WHEN: apply-patches.sh is idempotent (running twice produces identical output).
FIRST PROVING ACTION: tutor config save && apply-patches.sh && cp Dockerfile /tmp/pass1 && apply-patches.sh && diff /tmp/pass1 Dockerfile.

#1952 auto-closed 2026-04-21T00:40Z when #1925 merged with --delete-branch. The PR body said this was 'stacked on #1925'; base was fix/cold-start-onboarding-proof-20260420 which got deleted → GitHub closed the dependent PR.

The head branch (fix/build-proof-governance-followups-20260420 @ 94c54b77c) is still alive on remote with 3 genuine commits not yet on main:
- 1d73274fb — fix(onboarding): close bootstrap proof gaps (ALREADY-UPSTREAM — dropped by rebase)
- 69f76a61f — chore(governance): refresh branch protection debt review (ALREADY-UPSTREAM — dropped by rebase)
- 94c54b77c — fix(ci): pin helper images and refresh proof docs (GENUINE — keep)

Actually only 94c54b77c is unique post-rebase; the other 2 are from the #1925 squash.

## Recovery Steps
1. git worktree add /tmp/pr1952-recover --detach origin/fix/build-proof-governance-followups-20260420
2. git rebase --onto origin/main 59b6d6c07 HEAD
3. Resolve build-tutor-images.yml conflict (take DIND_HELPER_IMAGE rename, apply consistently to all 4 DinD job stanzas)
4. git push --force-with-lease origin HEAD:fix/build-proof-governance-followups-20260420
5. gh pr create --base main --head fix/build-proof-governance-followups-20260420

## Why I didn't auto-do this
/tmp/mereka-lms-next-proof-governance has ~30 uncommitted files from another concurrent session. Force-pushing would disrupt that session. Hand-off to whoever owns that worktree.

## Linked
- #1952 (closed)
- #1925 (merged 2026-04-21T00:40:04Z)
- #1951 (merged — introduced BUSYBOX_IMAGE env; #1952 wants to rename to DIND_HELPER_IMAGE)
close_reason: Stale. #1952 was superseded by #1957 (runbook) + #1958 (Stage 1) + #1959 (Stage 2 script). The BUSYBOX→DIND_HELPER_IMAGE rename concern was overtaken by gyce structural fix (bbi-infra #3565) which retires the shell step entirely (#1961). No recovery needed.
