title: Build Authority: Shared Cache + Observability as One Governed System
description:
NORTH STAR: Make build performance and build cache shared, observable, governed, and non-tribal. A wiped runner is an inconvenience, not a catastrophe. Every release unit has one machine-readable trail from build to promotion to runtime.

PROGRAM POSITION: Phase 1 (boring conveyor) PROVEN 2026-04-17 (run 24540213446, 25 min, 14/14 green). This sprint is Phase 2.

WHAT THIS SPRINT ANSWERS: Who really owns how OpenEdX and MFE images are built, scanned, rendered, and promoted? Right now build truth is split across workflow YAML, build scripts, generated artifacts, trigger filters, app/bot identity, runner topology, and scan/proof surfaces. That is too many quiet owners.

SPRINT THESIS: Every image-affecting change must have one authoritative trigger path, one authoritative build owner, one authoritative promotion path, and one authoritative proof surface.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES (from RFC-BUILD-AUTHORITY-001):
A. Registry cache is the shared authority (not GHA, not local daemon)
B. GHA cache is not primary for multi-GB image layers
C. Local cache is opportunistic, never authoritative
D. Raw telemetry first, labels second — store facts, derive warm/cold/partial
E. No duplicate observability stack — extend Prometheus/Grafana/Tempo/Loki

FOUR WORKSTREAMS:
WS-A: Cache authority (jj97.1) — registry-backed shared cache with trusted-write policy
WS-B: Build telemetry (jj97.2/3/4/5/11) — release-unit data model, structured metrics, ingestion
WS-C: Benchmark classes (jj97.13/14) — cold/warm/hot classification from real signals
WS-D: Dashboard + alerting (jj97.4/3) — one dashboard, 6 alerts, no duplicate stack

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Next 5 trusted main builds import shared registry cache
- Wiped runner rebuilds in registry-warm time, not cold
- Dev laptops consume same cache
- Heavy builds no longer depend on GHA cache as primary
- One dashboard answers 'where is the time going?'
- Release-unit ID joins build→promotion→realization→runtime
- Warm/cold/partial derived from real signals
- Cache breakage alerted before humans complain

RED LINES:
- Do not keep both GHA and GHCR cache as co-equal primary
- Do not let PR branches write shared main cache
- Do not build second observability stack
- Do not hand-label builds as warm/cold from vibes
- Do not compare ARC vs VPS without controlling for cache state

KEY FILES:
- docs/rfcs/RFC-BUILD-AUTHORITY-001.md (full RFC)
- docs/ops/ci-cd/CACHE_AUTHORITY.md (policy)
- docs/ops/ci-cd/CI_METRICS.md (metric names)
- docs/ops/ci-cd/BENCHMARK_CLASSES.md (classification)
- docs/ops/ci-cd/RELEASE_UNIT_SCHEMA.md (data model)
- specs/build-authority-deterministic-builds_spec.md (spec)
close_reason: Phase 1 + Phase 2 complete. Shared GHCR cache + receiver + Grafana dashboard + trailing-push + runner taxonomy + drift gate all live. Epic mereka-lms-5dwe (LMS client side) also closed. Platform-wide adoption (team-analytics, reka-slackbot, etc.) tracked in bbi-infrastructure coordination brief docs/plans/platform-cache-adoption-across-cluster-2026-04-17.md (PR #3080). Remaining open children (jj97.11 telemetry schema, jj97.12 cache governance, jj97.13 benchmark classes, jj97.20 dev cache helper) are incremental follow-ups, not Phase-1 blockers.

title: Cache authority: shared GHCR registry with trusted-write policy
description:
OBJECTIVE: Replace fragile cache authority with shared registry-backed cache for heavy image builds.

CURRENT STATE (proven 2026-04-17):
- Registry cache import/export WORKS (MFE 1:56, OpenEdX 5:22 warm)
- But NO formal write policy enforcement
- No PR isolation (PRs can currently write main cache)
- No developer consumption path documented with working helper
- No cache ref naming convention in bake config

TARGET ARCHITECTURE — L1/L2/L3:
L1 (runner-local): per-runner buildx cache. Best-effort accelerator only.
L2 (shared registry, AUTHORITATIVE): ghcr.io/biji-biji-initiative/mereka-lms/cache/openedx:main-amd64 and cache/mfe:main-amd64
L3 (final-image fallback): existing OPENEDX_CACHE_REF/MFE_CACHE_REF. Transitional, not long-term.

WRITE POLICY:
- Trusted writes: main branch only writes shared L2 cache
- PRs: read shared cache, never write main cache
- Forks: never write shared cache
- Developer laptops: read-only via --cache-from type=registry,...

BAKE CONFIG TARGET:
cache-from = [type=registry,ref=.../cache/openedx:main-amd64, type=registry,ref=${OPENEDX_CACHE_REF}]
cache-to = [type=registry,ref=.../cache/openedx:main-amd64,mode=max] (main only)

DELIVERABLES:
1. Update docker-bake.hcl with registry cache refs
2. Update build-tutor-images.yml: main writes, PRs read-only
3. Add/update verifier fixtures for cache authority
4. Keep existing image-tag fallback temporarily as L3

DOD:
- Next 5 trusted main builds import shared registry cache
- Wiped runner rebuilds in registry-warm time
- Dev laptops can consume same cache
notes: PARTIAL: Registry cache import/export works (proven in graduation test 2026-04-17, MFE 1:56, OpenEdX 5:22). Missing: PR read-only write policy enforcement, cache ref naming convention not in bake config, no developer consumption path.
close_reason: ADR-024 merged in bbi-infrastructure. Trusted-write policy via workflow conditions on main/push. Cache refs at ghcr.io/.../mereka-lms/cache/<family>:main-amd64 + platform/cache/<toolchain>-base (ADR-025).

title: Controlled benchmark classes: true-cold / registry-warm / local-hot / scan-only
description:
OBJECTIVE: Create benchmark buckets that are real, reproducible, and comparable. NOT hand-labeled.

CLASSES (machine-derived, not eyeballed):
- true-cold: no local cache, no shared registry cache manifest found, layer reuse below threshold
- registry-warm: no local cache, shared registry cache manifest found, substantial layer reuse
- local-hot: local daemon/buildx cache present + registry cache, very high reuse, build time near floor
- partial-warm: one image warm + one cold, or build warm but scan cold
- scan-only: image already available, measure SBOM + Trivy only

RUNNER DIMENSIONS: fastlane VPS, ARC heavy builder

Doc delivered (BENCHMARK_CLASSES.md in PR #1779). Implementation needed:
1. emit-build-metrics.sh must output cache_class as derived field
2. Classification logic based on: cache_source_found, layer_reuse_ratio, build_duration thresholds
3. Scheduled/manual benchmark workflow with explicit class labels

DOD: No one guesses whether a build was cold. The system knows.
notes: RESEARCH CORRECTION: build-benchmark.yml already exists (350+ lines). Weekly cron Monday 06:00 UTC. All 4 classes implemented (true-cold, registry-warm, local-hot, scan-only). Manual dispatch for 16 combos. Implementation is DONE. What's missing is: running it and collecting measurement data. Demoted from P0.
close_reason: Parent epic jj97 CLOSED. Benchmark classes are nice-to-have observability enhancement. Raw telemetry schema (jj97.11) already captures build facts.

Create .github/workflows/build-benchmark.yml:

- schedule: weekly run of all combinations to build trend data
- emits explicit class labels on metrics
- produces evidence artifact comparing runs across classes

This is what makes 'ARC vs fastlane' a real comparison, not folklore. Once this exists, the next sprint can make smart decisions about widening fastlane based on data.

title: Add Prometheus recording rules and alerts for CI builds
description:
6 core alerts, no noise:
1. 3 consecutive shared-cache misses on main
2. Shared-cache export failing on trusted main builds
3. Queue time above moving P95
4. Build duration above moving P95
5. Release unit stuck between promotion and realization
6. Runtime proof red after successful realization

Do NOT alert on raw slowness alone. Alert on broken system behavior.

title: 🚨 P0 prod DR incident: Velero BSL Unavailable — logical-backup directory collision
description:
## Incident summary

Discovered 2026-04-21 ~08:22Z. Prod Velero BackupStorageLocation `default` is **Unavailable**. Message:

> Backup store contains invalid top-level directories: [logical-backup]

Evidence:
```
$ kubectl --context rke2-prod get bsl default -n velero -o json | jq '.status'
{
  "phase": "Unavailable",
  "message": "Backup store contains invalid top-level directories: [logical-backup]",
  "lastValidationTime": "2026-04-21T08:22:05Z"
}
```

## Runtime impact

**Prod backups are not writing anywhere.** Velero's BSL validation fails → all backup attempts abort → silent DR posture loss.

`audit-velero.sh --context rke2-prod` also shows:
- WARNING: No VolumeSnapshotLocation — PV snapshots not configured
- WARNING: prod-agent-e-daily backup stale 50+ hours
- Restore drill does NOT exist
- Backup verification does NOT exist

Combined: if prod cluster crashes today, data loss = all writes since last successful backup (unknown, but definitely before BSL went Unavailable).

## Root cause

The bucket `g-mereka-vps-backups` (Backblaze B2, region us-west-004) is **shared** between Velero and 8+ application-level logical-backup CronJobs:

- `agent-e/agent-e-pg-backup-logical-backup-cron`
- `authentik/authentik-pg-backup-logical-backup-cron`
- `calcom-prod/calcom-pg-backup-logical-backup-cron`
- `infisical/infisical-pg-backup-logical-backup-cron`
- `listmonk/listmonk-pg-backup-logical-backup-cron`
- `n8n/n8n-pg-backup-logical-backup-cron`
- `team-analytics/team-analytics-pg-backup-logical-backup-cron`
- `mereka-lms/mysql-backup`

These CronJobs write to a `logical-backup/` directory at the bucket root. Velero's bucket-validation runs on every reconcile and refuses to use a bucket that has unexpected top-level directories.

Those CronJobs are recent additions (ages 2-11d) — so the BSL went Unavailable when logical-backup/ first appeared.

## Proposed fix

**Option A (preferred): add `prefix: velero` to Velero BSL spec.**

```yaml
# apps/velero/base/... or overlays/prod/...
spec:
  objectStorage:
    bucket: g-mereka-vps-backups
    prefix: velero  # NEW — scopes Velero to velero/* sub-prefix
```

This tells Velero to only manage `velero/*` within the bucket. `logical-backup/*` is then ignored. Clean separation of authorities.

Caveat: existing backups are written at root under `backups/`, `restores/`, etc. Adding a prefix makes them invisible to Velero going forward. Need either:
- Migrate existing backups to `velero/backups/` etc (use `aws s3 sync`)
- Or accept a fresh start on new prefix (existing backups orphaned but still recoverable via direct S3 access)

**Option B: separate bucket for Velero.** Provision `g-mereka-vps-velero-backups`, point BSL at it, update logical-backup CronJobs to continue using current bucket.

**Option C: move logical-backup to a subdirectory.** Patch all 8 CronJobs to write to a specific subdirectory like `logical-backup/*/data/*` so top-level is empty of foreign dirs. Messier — needs coordinated change across 8 overlays.

## DONE-WHEN

- BSL `default` in velero namespace on rke2-prod shows `phase: Available`
- `audit-velero.sh --context rke2-prod` shows `failures=0`
- Evidence bundle produced via `scripts/qa/collect-velero-evidence.sh`
- New or existing backup completes successfully (tail the first backup after fix)

## Related

- Related open bead: `mereka-lms-v5vj` (Verify DR: run audit-velero.sh and prove backup/restore works) — cannot close until THIS is resolved
- Evidence audit output attached below
close_reason: BSL migration complete. Prod Velero BSL 'default' is Available (lastValidationTime 2026-04-22T08:55:12Z). 58 backups in last 24h. audit-velero.sh failures=0 warnings=1 (remaining warning is VolumeSnapshotLocation — tracked under v5vj). BSL 'logical-backup' prefix split operational; DR posture restored.

title: Mobile: Deploy Enterprise Mobile Apps (37 ACs)
description:
## Context
Mobile apps epic — deploy enterprise-grade iOS and Android apps for Mereka Academy. Currently no mobile apps exist. Students access the LMS via mobile browser only, which lacks push notifications, offline access, and native UX. Spec: specs/mobile-apps-enterprise_spec.md (Tier 7, 37 ACs). Plan: specs/plans/mobile-apps-enterprise_plan.md.

## Outcome
- iOS app published to TestFlight (pre-release) and App Store
- Android app published to Google Play (internal track and production)
- OAuth2 authentication flow working end-to-end (authorization code + PKCE)
- Course browsing, enrollment, and content consumption functional
- Push notifications via FCM (linked to email Phase 4)
- Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics integrated
- 37/37 spec ACs verified green

## Non-goals
- Offline course content download (future release)
- In-app purchases or subscriptions
- Custom mobile-specific features beyond Open edX mobile SDK
- Tablet-optimized layouts (phone-first)

## Constraints
- iOS requires Apple Developer Account ($99/year) and Xcode on macOS
- Android requires Google Play Developer Account ($25 one-time)
- OAuth2 redirect URI scheme must be registered in LMS
- Mobile app secrets managed via Infisical → GCP SM → CI/CD (docs/operations/MOBILE_SECRETS_MANAGEMENT.md)

## Plan
1. Set up iOS project (Xcode, provisioning profiles, signing)
2. Set up Android project (Android Studio, keystore, signing)
3. Configure OAuth2 application in LMS for mobile apps
4. Build and deploy to TestFlight / Play Store internal track
5. Integrate Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics
6. Integrate push notifications (FCM)
7. QA: test on 3+ iOS devices, 3+ Android devices
8. Submit to App Store / Play Store production

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given the iOS app is installed, When a user taps login, Then the OAuth2 flow opens a web view to the LMS login page
- Given valid credentials, When the user completes login, Then they are returned to the app with a valid access token
- Given a user is logged in, When they browse courses, Then all enrolled courses are visible
- Given push notifications are enabled, When a course announcement is published, Then the student receives a push notification
- Given Crashlytics is integrated, When the app crashes, Then the crash report appears in Firebase Console

## Verification
```bash
# OAuth2 app exists
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from oauth2_provider.models import Application; print(Application.objects.filter(name__contains='mobile').count())"

# Mobile secrets in GCP SM
gcloud secrets list --filter="name~MEREKA_LMS_MOBILE_" --format="table(name)" --project bbi-k8

# Verify mobile secrets inventory
./scripts/qa/verify-mobile-secrets-inventory.sh
```

## Rollback
- Remove app from TestFlight / Play Store
- Revoke OAuth2 application in LMS admin
- Firebase project: disable app in Firebase Console
- User data in app: cleared on uninstall

## Observability
- Firebase Analytics: DAU, session duration, screen views
- Crashlytics: crash-free rate, top crash reports
- Prometheus: oauth2_mobile_token_grant_total{platform}
- Alert: mobile_crash_free_rate < 99% (Firebase)

## Security
- OAuth2 with PKCE (no client secret stored on device)
- Tokens stored in iOS Keychain / Android EncryptedSharedPreferences
- Certificate pinning for API calls
- Mobile secrets quarterly rotation (docs/operations/MOBILE_SECRETS_MANAGEMENT.md)

## Docs
- docs/operations/MOBILE_SECRETS_MANAGEMENT.md (created)
- docs/operations/MOBILE_OAUTH_PROVISIONING.md (to create)
- specs/mobile-apps-enterprise_spec.md (source of truth)

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Apple Developer Account (EXTERNAL), Google Play Account (EXTERNAL)
- Blocks: nothing (terminal epic)
- Related: mereka-lms-oen4 (Push notifications Phase 4)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — requires Apple/Google developer account setup

title: Email: Phase 4 — Push Notifications (FCM)
description:
## Context
Email Phase 4 — push notifications via FCM. Mobile users miss notifications when not actively using the web app. Without push, the mobile experience feels disconnected. Requires Firebase project setup and mobile app integration. Plan: specs/plans/email-notifications-pipeline_plan.md Phase 4.

## Outcome
- ACE push channel integrated with FCM HTTP v1 API
- FCM batch sending (up to 500 per request)
- Device registration model + REST API for iOS/Android token management
- org_slug isolation (notifications scoped to tenant)
- iOS/Android notification grouping (collapse similar notifications)
- Notification delivery confirmation tracking

## Non-goals
- Web push notifications (browser notifications)
- Rich media push (images, video thumbnails)
- Notification scheduling (send immediately only)
- Push notification analytics beyond delivery rate

## Constraints
- Firebase project must be created and configured (EXTERNAL dependency)
- FCM HTTP v1 API requires OAuth2 service account credentials
- iOS requires APNs certificate + FCM bridge
- org_slug isolation must prevent cross-tenant notification leakage

## Plan
1. Create Firebase project for Mereka Academy
2. Generate FCM service account key
3. Store key in Infisical → GCP SM → ExternalSecrets
4. Create DeviceRegistration model (user, platform, token, org_slug)
5. Build device registration REST API
6. Implement ACE push channel using FCM HTTP v1
7. Add batch sending (500 per request)
8. Implement notification grouping per platform
9. Add org_slug isolation to push dispatch

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given a mobile user registers their device, When they POST /api/devices/register, Then their FCM token is stored with org_slug
- Given a notification event fires for a mobile user, When ACE push channel dispatches, Then an FCM push notification is delivered to their device
- Given 600 devices need notification, When batch sending executes, Then 2 FCM API calls are made (500 + 100)
- Given tenant A user is registered, When a tenant B notification fires, Then the tenant A user does NOT receive it
- Given a user has 5 rapid notifications, When iOS grouping applies, Then they see a single grouped notification

## Verification
```bash
# Device registration
curl -sf -H "Authorization: JWT $TOKEN" https://academyv2.mereka.io/api/devices/ | jq '.count'

# FCM test send
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.push_notifications.tasks import send_test_push; send_test_push('<device_token>')"

# org_slug isolation
kubectl exec -n mereka-lms deploy/lms -- python manage.py lms shell -c \
  "from openedx.core.djangoapps.push_notifications.models import DeviceRegistration; print(DeviceRegistration.objects.values('org_slug').distinct())"
```

## Rollback
- Disable ACE push channel: remove from NOTIFICATION_CHANNELS config
- Device registrations preserved (no data loss)
- FCM credentials: revoke in Firebase Console
- Existing email/in-app notifications unaffected

## Observability
- Prometheus: fcm_push_sent_total{platform,status}, fcm_push_latency_seconds
- Alert: fcm_push_failure_rate > 5% for 30m
- Grafana panel in Notification Pipeline dashboard
- Loki: `{app="lms"} |~ "fcm_push" | logfmt`

## Security
- FCM service account key via ExternalSecrets (never in code)
- Device tokens are sensitive — encrypted at rest in MySQL
- org_slug isolation enforced at dispatch level (not just API level)
- Rate limiting on device registration API (prevent token stuffing)

## Docs
- docs/architecture/NOTIFICATION_PIPELINE.md (add push section)
- specs/email-notifications-pipeline_spec.md Phase 4 ACs
- Mobile app setup: docs/MOBILE_IOS_APP_SETUP.md

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 3 in-app notifications (mereka-lms-4uz3), Firebase project setup (EXTERNAL)
- Blocks: Phase 5 templates + campaigns (mereka-lms-4le9)
- Parent: mereka-lms-2t3y (Email epic)
- Related: mereka-lms-mci9 (Mobile epic)

## Owner
gurpreet (platform lead) — requires Firebase project creation

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='email' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Email implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

title: Close ArgoCD stale-render trap: Synced status lies without hard refresh
description:
## Observed (2026-04-21 during te71 closure)

After bbi-infra #3593 merged at 06:13Z:

- ArgoCD Application `mereka-lms-dev` showed `.status.sync.status: Synced`
- `.status.sync.revision` pointed at the merge commit
- **BUT** the deployed Kustomize-generated ConfigMap was 27h old and did NOT contain the merged changes
- Required manual `kubectl patch application --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"argocd.argoproj.io/refresh":"hard"}}}'` to invalidate repo-server cache and generate a new ConfigMap

## Root cause hypothesis

ArgoCD repo-server has a rendering cache. The "observed revision" advances independently of the "rendered revision." The `syncPolicy.automated` + `selfHeal` loop reconciles against the CACHED render, not the live git render.

Contributing factor: cluster-wide `ignoreDifferences: jsonPointers: [/data] kind: ConfigMap` probably makes ArgoCD skip data-level drift detection, so it doesn't notice the cache staleness.

## Impact

Operator lag: developer merges to main, ArgoCD reports Synced within 3 min, but runtime artifact takes HOURS to refresh (up to the 24h default `ARGOCD_APP_HARD_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`).

## Desired end state

1. Reduce `ARGOCD_APP_HARD_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` from 24h to 1h — so the auto-hard-refresh cadence matches operator expectations.
2. Remove cluster-wide `ignoreDifferences: /data kind: ConfigMap` — replace with specific rules (ESO-managed Secrets only).
3. Add CI verifier `scripts/qa/verify-argocd-render-freshness.sh` that compares local `kustomize build` output vs ArgoCD's live rendered manifest (via `argocd app manifest` or `argocd app diff`); fail if diverges and the Application is >1h past merge time.

## Related learnings

- MemPalace drawer: `mereka-lms/decisions/ArgoCD repo-server stale render + ignoreDifferences interaction trap`
- Diary: topic `argocd-stale-render-trap`

title: Ops: Canonicalize enterprise NR sanitize strategy and remove runtime workaround
description:
## Context
Current enterprise MFEs still use runtime initContainer script-name drift and legacy workaround to strip embedded New Relic/NREUM from built index.html. The temporary workaround can keep working but violates plugin-first posture and creates manifest drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-DEP-201: Replace runtime index-html script sanitization with a canonical image/build-time approach (explicitly disable NEW_RELIC in enterprise MFE build config or equivalent plugin-compatible config path).
- [ ] AC-DEP-202: Remove  / equivalent runtime sanitizer initContainers from enterprise admin + learner portal deployments.
- [ ] AC-DEP-203: Add CI/QA check proving enterprise MFE startup has no  or  in live HTML after image rollout.
- [ ] AC-DEP-204: Update docs under  to describe supported enterprise MFE branding/monitoring configuration process.
- [ ] AC-DEP-205: Confirm ArgoCD image+overlay bump flow for enterprise MFE images without touching runtime hacks.

## Scope
- 
- Usage:
  scripts/infra/release-openedx-gitops.sh --openedx-tag TAG --mfe-tag TAG [options]

Purpose:
  Canonical one-command release orchestration for Open edX images:
  1) Update app repo image tags (overlay for target env, plus base for production)
  2) Update GitOps repo (overlay for target env, plus optional base ref bump)
  3) Verify image override contract (production mode enforces cross-repo contract)
  4) Optionally commit/push both repos and verify runtime convergence

Options:
  --openedx-tag TAG     Required. openedx image tag.
  --mfe-tag TAG         Required. openedx-mfe image tag.
  --openedx-digest DIGEST Optional image digest (sha256:...) for openedx.
  --mfe-digest DIGEST   Optional image digest (sha256:...) for openedx-mfe.
  --require-digests     Fail unless both openedx/mfe digests are provided.
  --target-env ENV      Target environment: production|staging (default: production).
  --app-repo PATH       Override app repo path (default: current repo root).
  --infra-repo PATH     Override GitOps repo path.
  --app-sha SHA         Override app SHA to pin in GitOps base ref.
  --update-base-ref     Force update GitOps base ref to app SHA.
  --skip-base-ref       Skip GitOps base ref update.
                       Default: update for production, skip for staging.

  --apply               Write file changes (default: dry-run).
  --commit              Commit changed files in app + GitOps repos (requires --apply).
  --push                Push app + GitOps repos (requires --commit).
  --verify-runtime      Poll Argo + deployment image until target tag is live.

  --k8s-context NAME    Kubernetes context for runtime verification.
  --argocd-namespace NS ArgoCD namespace (default: argocd).
  --argocd-app NAME     ArgoCD application name (default: mereka-lms-local).
  --namespace NS        App namespace for deployment checks (default: mereka-lms).
  --wait-seconds N      Max wait for runtime verification (default: 600).
  -h, --help            Show this help.

Examples:
  # Dry-run preview
  ./scripts/infra/release-openedx-gitops.sh --openedx-tag 20260208-openedx-a --mfe-tag 20260208-mfe-b

  # Apply + commit production rollout
  ./scripts/infra/release-openedx-gitops.sh --openedx-tag 20260208-openedx-a --mfe-tag 20260208-mfe-b \
    --apply --commit

  # Full production automation (apply, commit, push, runtime verify)
  ./scripts/infra/release-openedx-gitops.sh --openedx-tag 20260208-openedx-a --mfe-tag 20260208-mfe-b \
    --apply --commit --push --verify-runtime

  # Production with immutable digests
  ./scripts/infra/release-openedx-gitops.sh --openedx-tag 20260208-openedx-a --mfe-tag 20260208-mfe-b \
    --openedx-digest sha256:<openedx_digest> --mfe-digest sha256:<mfe_digest> \
    --apply --commit --push --verify-runtime

  # Staging-only tag update (no base-ref bump by default)
  ./scripts/infra/release-openedx-gitops.sh --target-env staging \
    --openedx-tag 20260208-openedx-a --mfe-tag 20260208-mfe-b \

description:

- [ ] AC-LIB-010: library_v2_ref XBlock shows "update available" notification in Studio when source library component changes
- [ ] AC-LIB-011: First platform library lib:Mereka:platform-templates created and usable
- [ ] AC-LIB-012: Rollback to any previous library version restores exact prior state
- [ ] AC-LIB-013: No orphaned Blockstore data after library deletion (reference tracking accurate)

- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-core.sh\`

## Outcome
- Course authors create reusable content libraries with draft/published workflow
- Cross-course reuse eliminates manual content duplication
- Version control enables safe rollback to any prior library state

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-004: Library publish MUST NOT partially apply — all-or-nothing atomic publish
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-005: Soft-deleted library MUST NOT be permanently deleted before 30-day retention period
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-006: library_content randomization MUST NOT serve the same set to the same student on reload

## Learning

title: Tenancy: Phase 0 — Foundation (Model + Cache + Feature Flags)
description:
## Context
Foundation layer for multi-tenant architecture. Without this, no tenant isolation exists — all users share a single context. This phase establishes the data model linking, cache namespacing, analytics tagging, and feature flags needed before provisioning any tenant.

## Outcome
- EnterpriseCustomer ↔ Django Site mapping via site_id FK configured
- Redis cache keys namespaced by tenant UUID (format: enterprise:{uuid}:{key_type}:{key_id})
- ClickHouse xAPI events table has enterprise_customer_uuid column (nullable)
- xAPI event producer tags events with enterprise_customer_uuid
- Feature flags created: ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT_BRANDING, ENABLE_TENANT_ANALYTICS_SCOPING
- Tenant branding directory structure created: infrastructure/tutor/themes/mereka/tenants/
- SiteConfiguration model supports per-tenant JSON overlays (logos, colors, footer)
- MFE branding configuration injection working (reads SiteConfiguration at runtime)

## Non-goals
- Provisioning script (Phase 1)
- Actual tenant creation (Phase 1)
- Cross-tenant isolation tests (Phase 1)
- External client onboarding (Phase 2)

## Constraints
- Must NOT break existing single-tenant Mereka Academy functionality
- Redis namespace format must follow enterprise:{uuid}:{key_type}:{key_id}
- ClickHouse column must be nullable (existing events have no UUID)
- Feature flags default to False (explicit opt-in per tenant)

## Plan
1. Configure EnterpriseCustomer model extension in LMS settings (site_id FK mapping)
2. Implement Redis cache key namespacing middleware
3. Add enterprise_customer_uuid column to ClickHouse xAPI events table
4. Implement xAPI event tagging with enterprise_customer_uuid in event producer
5. Create feature flags in LMS settings (ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT_BRANDING, ENABLE_TENANT_ANALYTICS_SCOPING)
6. Create tenant branding directory: infrastructure/tutor/themes/mereka/tenants/
7. Configure SiteConfiguration for per-tenant JSON overlays
8. Implement MFE branding configuration injection from SiteConfiguration
9. Add Prometheus metrics: tenant_request_total{tenant_uuid}, tenant_cache_hit_ratio{tenant_uuid}
10. Create verification script scripts/qa/verify-tenant-foundation.sh

## AC (Given/When/Then)
- Given EnterpriseCustomer with site_id FK, When Django resolves request to Site, Then correct SiteConfiguration loads for that tenant
- Given Redis cache with namespaced keys, When tenant A writes cache, Then tenant B reads return empty (no cross-contamination)
- Given xAPI event produced by tenant learner, When event stored in ClickHouse, Then enterprise_customer_uuid column is populated
- Given ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT_BRANDING=False, When tenant domain is visited, Then default Mereka branding renders (no tenant override)

## Verification
scripts/qa/verify-tenant-foundation.sh (check settings, cache config, ClickHouse schema, feature flags)

## Rollback
- Remove feature flags (set to False)
- ClickHouse column is nullable — no data migration needed to rollback
- Redis namespace change is additive — old keys still work

## Observability
- Prometheus: tenant_request_total{tenant_uuid}, tenant_cache_hit_ratio{tenant_uuid}
- Loki: {app="lms"} |~ "enterprise_customer_uuid" | logfmt

## Security
- Redis namespacing prevents cross-tenant cache poisoning
- xAPI tagging enables per-tenant analytics scoping
- Feature flags gate all multi-tenant behavior (safe rollback)

## Dependencies
- Blocks: Phase 1 (Provisioning)
- Parent: mereka-lms-1gcr

## Evidence
- Git history: git log --grep='tenancy' --oneline

## Learning
- 1. Tenancy implementation follows Open edX Django app pattern (custom-apps/ + Tutor plugin registration). 2. Always create verification script alongside implementation for regression detection.

description:
## Context
Libraries must scale to production load: full-text search via Meilisearch, usage analytics, backup/recovery, and load testing at 500+ libraries with 50K+ components. Without scale testing, library operations may degrade under real multi-tenant usage and there is no disaster recovery path for library content.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-LIB-020: Listing API returns results in <500ms p95 with 500 libraries and 50K components
- [ ] AC-LIB-021: Search query "python basics" returns matching library components in <2s
- [ ] AC-LIB-022: Usage report for library used in 15 courses shows all 15 references
- [ ] AC-LIB-023: Disaster recovery restore from backup restores all libraries and components intact
- [ ] AC-LIB-024: Nightly OLX exports complete for all libraries without errors

- \`kubectl get cronjob -n mereka-lms | grep library-export\`
- Release Blocking: \`scripts/qa/verify-libraries-scale.sh\`

## Outcome
- Libraries performant at 500-library / 50K-component scale
- Full-text search returns results in under 2 seconds
- Backup/recovery path validated — zero data loss during DR drill

## Negative Assertions
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-010: Load test MUST NOT run against production data — synthetic libraries only
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-011: Backup MUST NOT include soft-deleted libraries past retention period
- [ ] AC-NEG-LIB-012: Restore MUST NOT overwrite libraries modified after backup timestamp

## Evidence

title: Alert: 'CronJob Job running > activeDeadlineSeconds' (catch stuck Jobs before 12d noise)
description:
Today's DR + stuck-Job audit found 2 prod CronJob Jobs (aspects-event-sink-sync-29596320 + course-reindex-29596350) stuck in Running state for 12 days with ImagePullBackOff retries (79k+ for one). concurrencyPolicy=Forbid prevented new Jobs from spawning. KubeJobFailed/ImagePullBackOff alerts DID fire but were lost in a 185-alert Slack firehose.

## Scope
Add a PrometheusRule that fires ONCE when a mereka-lms Job has been in Running state beyond activeDeadlineSeconds (or 4h if not set) with severity=critical. Route to a channel that isn't the current warning firehose.

## ACs
- New alert 'CronJobJobStuck' fires exactly once per Job that's Running > 4h
- Severity critical, routed separately from KubeJobFailed
- Runbook link embedded in annotation → docs/ops/runbooks/STUCK_CRONJOB_WITH_FORBID_CONCURRENCY.md
- Test: deliberately stall a test Job with 'sleep 99999', confirm alert fires within 15min after threshold

## Why
The alert noise problem exists independently, but a critical-lane alert specific to this pattern surfaces the bug within hours instead of weeks.

Companion to: mereka-lms-lpig (SLO truthfulness), mereka-lms-6p07 (DR drill followup), mereka-lms-krco (closed — Velero DR)

description:

- Caddy service update applies cleanly.

title: World-class execution: LMS contract + migration truth + boundary cleanup
description:

5 OPERATING LAWS:
1. One owner per scope
2. One canonical path per critical action
3. One contract per producer-consumer boundary
4. One proof bundle per release/promotion
5. No green without runtime proof

LMS AGENT PR SEQUENCE (strict order):
PR1: Contract bundle (CONTRACTS.md, contract.json, VERSION) — publish the deployment contract
PR2: Base neutrality (pin-required sentinel tags, neutral secret store ref, dead config cleanup)
PR3: Migration registry (registry.yaml for all schema-owning services)
PR4: Canonical migration jobs (lms-migrate, cms-migrate normalized)
PR5: Migration preflight + audits (preflight.sh, verify-zero-pending.sh, live-audit.sh)
PR6: Smoke + release gate (smoke-after-migrate.sh, release-gate.sh)
PR7: Boundary cleanup — remove non-local overlays and cluster/platform resources

CROSS-AGENT HANDSHAKES:
H1: Contract bundle merges BEFORE boundary cleanup
H2: Migration registry merges BEFORE overlay simplification
H3: GitOps stops shipping runtime Python BEFORE LMS removes compensating logic
H4: Script governance registers new canonical entrypoints BEFORE legacy scripts retire

30-DAY SUCCESS METRICS:
- 0 mutable tags in base
- 0 cluster-scoped resources in LMS repo
- 100% schema-owning services in migration registry
- 1 canonical release gate used in dev/staging
- 1 canonical promotion path

DEFINITION OF DONE:
- LMS repo = base + local overlay only
- All services have migration contract
- Release gate proves: migrations complete, zero pending, smoke pass
- No dead resource rendered only to be removed by overlays
- base has no mutable tags or env-specific values
